articles.title: Premier League Says Manchester City Inflated Revenues By $1 Billion Using 'Sham Contracts'
articles.summary: The Premier League issued a statement addressing the "serious breaches" of financial rules committed by Manchester City between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.
articles.body:
The Premier League issued a statement addressing the "serious breaches" of financial rules committed by Manchester City between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The league said Manchester City "arranged 'sham' contracts" with commercial partners and "filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances."

This was done to make sure City remained with the spending limits laid out by the Premier League and UEFA, which oversees the Champions League and other continental competitions.

The Premier League alleged City's balance sheet was off by £900 million (nearly $1.2 billion) during the period in question.

Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano declined to respond to questions from Sky News' Rob Harris about the Premier League's findings:

The club released its own statement , saying it's "both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission."

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

Manchester City won three Premier League titles and an FA Cup during the years that were scrutinized. While the club's most dominant period followed the 2017-18 season, the alleged financial breaches will have helped City lay the groundwork for Pep Guardiola's arrival in 2016 and everything it achieved with him in the dugout.

In terms of repercussions, retroactive action may not be all that satisfying for rival clubs.

Tony Pulis, who managed Stoke City in the 2011 FA Cup final, wrote in a BBC Sport column that "I still feel cheated."

"Whatever happens next, we won't ever get that day back and the chance to celebrate around Stoke-on-Trent with the cup and medals we so honestly fought for," he said. "After breaking the rules, Manchester City got to do that instead."

But the Premier League is likely to face plenty of pressure to levy a punishment that fits the alleged crimes.

articles.title: Barrios, un regreso progresivo
articles.standfirst: El canterano trabajó junto a sus compañeros cerca de 40 minutos
articles.summary: El canterano trabajó junto a sus compañeros cerca de 40 minutos
articles.body: Es la gran noticia del parón internacional. Pablo Barrios está de vuelta. El canterano trabajó junto al resto de compañeros de la primera plantilla que no han viajado con sus selecciones. El centrocampista se unió a Koke, Llorente, Cardoso, Arnau y Dani Martínez en una sesión en la que volvió a estar ausente Sorloth. Mientras Barrios fue la noticia positiva al entrenar durante unos 40 minutos al mismo ritmo que los demás, el noruego sigue recuperándose de su lesión en el gimnasio. Con prácticamente todo el equipo con sus selecciones, hasta 17 internacionales tiene el Atlético en este parón, los de Simeone regresaron al trabajo tras tres días de descanso. Con el regreso de Barrios, el Cholo recupera así a uno de sus futbolistas más diferenciales. El canterano se ha perdido los últimos tres encuentros ante Real Sociedad, Osasuna y el derbi ante el Real Madrid. Ya el pasado viernes se dejó ver en uno de los campos anexos trabajando en solitario y hoy ha participado en el comienzo de la sesión. Grandes noticias para Simeone. Barrios, que entrenó al mismo ritmo que sus compañeros aunque por un espacio menor de tiempo, si no hay ningún contratiempo, debería estar listo para el siguiente partido del Atlético, el 10 de octubre en Vitoria. Tiempo suficiente para afinar la puesta a punto de uno de los pilares del Atlético.

articles.title: El Barça vuelve a su Liga
articles.standfirst: Visita Roma en la segunda jornada de la fase Liga de la UWCL con el regreso de Van Asten y las campeonas del mundo Sub'20 como principales novedades
articles.summary: Visita Roma en la segunda jornada de la fase Liga de la UWCL con el regreso de Van Asten y las campeonas del mundo Sub'20 como principales novedades
articles.body: El Barcelona visita este miércoles (18:45 horas) el Stadio Tre Fontane para medirse a la Roma en la segunda jornada de la fase Liga de la Women's Champions League. Tras la goleada de la primera fecha frente al Paris FC, el equipo dirigido por Pere Romeu busca mantener su estatus ante un equipo al que ha ganado en las tres ocasiones que se han enfrentado. "Esto es la Champions y jugar fuera de casa no es fácil. Tenemos que sacar una muy buena versión para conseguir los tres puntos", apuntó el técnico. El 21 de marzo de 2023, el Barcelona se impuso por la mínima (0-1) en el Olímpico de Roma gracias a un gol de Salma Paralluelo. Ocho días más tarde, las azulgrana rubricaron el pase a las semifinales del torneo con una goleada (5-1) en el Camp Nou con tantos de Fridolina Rolfö (2), Mapi León, Asisat Oshoala y Patri Guijarro. La última vez que se enfrentaron, hará ahora un año, tuvo como escenario de juego el Stadio Tre Fontane y acabó con triunfo azulgrana (0-4) con goles de Esmee Brugts, Kika Nazareth, Alexia Putellas y Caroline Graham. "La Roma es un gran equipo, que hasta ahora con este entrenador que tienen de esta temporada es un equipo agresivo en presiones altas, es un equipo que le gusta jugar en campos rivales", analizó Romeu. La novedad en la convocatoria azulgrana es el regreso de Renee van Asten, ausente por lesión (miofascial posterior del recto anterior derecho) en los últimos cinco choques de su equipo. "Hemos tenido un tramo inicial de temporada con dificultades. Doy mucho valor al trabajo hecho este septiembre, ya que hemos tenido poca disponibilidad de jugadoras", destacó el técnico, que cuenta con el regreso de las campeonas del mundo Sub'20 Carla Julià, Aïcha Camara, Noa Jiménez, y Rosalía Domínguez. "Aunque aún tenemos bajas, volvemos a ser nosotras como equipo", añadió. "Aun estando en Polonia, estábamos muy pendientes del equipo, las hemos ido viendo. Estamos recuperando jugadoras, vamos creciendo", subrayó Julià. El Barcelona pone el foco en Europa, en Roma concretamente, pero es imposible no pensar también en el Clásico ante el Real Madrid del próximo domingo en el Camp Nou.

articles.title: Brazil to bring security team to avoid Messi-like fiasco
articles.summary: Panaji: The Brazil national football team has been assured of top-notch security by authorities in India, but the five-time world champions are not
articles.body: Panaji: The Brazil national football team has been assured of top-notch security by authorities in India, but the five-time world champions are not leaving anything to chance.An eight-member security delegation from Brazil will arrive in Kolkata before the national team to ensure that the star footballers are well protected when they step into the country.A star-studded Brazilian squad captained by Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) defender Marquinhos and including Real Madrid attacker Vinicius Junior, Barcelona forward Raphinha, and Arsenal pair Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimaraes will arrive in Kolkata on Oct 1.The Selecao will play a friendly against India on Oct 3.“Brazil will have a security team comprising experts and former Army officials,” a source who is involved in organisation of the match told TOI. “They will be in Kolkata early on Wednesday, much before the team arrives. Their job is to ensure the safety of the players, delegates, and work with the police to ensure that security is as per international standards.”Last December, Lionel Messi’s visit to the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata during the India tour descended into mayhem as angry fans ripped up seats and invaded the field, prompting the Argentina superstar to cut short his visit. Thousands of fans were angry as their view of the star footballer was blocked by dozens of VIPs and organisers who were seen jostling for a selfie.“Extra precautions are being taken,” said another official.The hotel where Brazil will stay for three days will be turned into a fortress. According to sources, the Brazil football federation (CBF) has asked for a “secure training centre, situated no more than 25 minutes travelling time from the hotel and 24-hour security on all floors of the hotel where the team will stay.”At the stadium, restrooms and other public facilities are being renovated, while new fencing is being installed around the practice grounds as part of the security arrangements.Brazil played two friendlies against Australia as part of their Asia tour and are now headed to India for a historic clash against India. The former world champions are ranked fifth in the world, while India are at 137.Last week, India held World Cuppers Panama, ranked world no. 40, to a 1-1 draw at the Sree Kanteerava stadium in Bengaluru.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Laporta: "El Madrid compareció en el Caso Negreira para alargar el caso y justificar la actuación de su TV"
articles.standfirst: El presidente reconoce que la relación con el eterno rival es, a día de hoy, inexistente"
articles.summary: El presidente reconoce que la relación con el eterno rival es, a día de hoy, inexistente"
articles.body: Joan Laporta aprovechó la Asamblea celebrada en Copenhague de la European Football Clubs (EFC) para lanzar un duro mensaje contra el eterno rival, el Real Madrid, por sus constantes ataques al Barça por el 'caso Negreira'. En declaraciones a "Mundo Deportivo", el máximo mandatario azulgrana también desvela un acercamiento con el Atlético de Madrid. "Lo que no podemos aceptar es que se falte a la verdad y cada vez que intervienen públicamente, pues se metan con el Barça. Nuestro departamento legal reacciona ante estas situaciones. Lo hacemos con todos los que nos han condenado antes de juzgarnos y han dicho cosas que no eran ciertas, y seguimos en la misma tónica. Yo lo que espero es que se rectifique y que esto se solvente. Con el Madrid ya sabéis que se han roto relaciones, ellos comparecieron en el caso Negreira, entendemos que solo para alargar el caso y justificar una actuación de su televisión y un discurso que tienen predeterminado. Y ahí es donde hay confrontación y la relación existente es cero". "Hemos pensado, cuando nos vimos, que teníamos que continuar la buena relación que hay entre los dos clubs y la personal que tenemos. Yo lo aprecio mucho, él lo sabe, noto también su cariño y nos vimos y enseguida nos dimos un abrazo y creo que hemos limado asperezas y que hemos retomado la relación como debe ser. Y estoy muy satisfecho porque además es una persona que aprecio mucho". "Ya sabéis que yo, como culé y como presidente del Barça, quiero que gane un jugador del Barça. Hay muchos que son candidatos y estamos muy orgullosos. Y si es Lamine Yamal, pues estaré muy feliz, porque hizo una gran temporada, está divirtiendo al mundo del fútbol constantemente con sus actuaciones. Ha empezado muy bien esta temporada también, sigue a un alto nivel. Es de esos jugadores que, como él mismo dice, divierte al espectador y ya veremos qué pasa el día 26, pero confiamos que se haga justicia y que gane un jugador del Barça. Y si es Lamine estaremos muy felices". "Aquí hay ahora preocupación por estas paradas, que casi son una pretemporada. Lo que refiere al fútbol de selección se ve con cierta preocupación porque es muy fácil que se produzcan lesiones, como así está siendo y desgraciadamente en el Barça, pues hemos sufrido ya una lesión parece ser que leve de Eric García y he tenido noticias de que han tenido que sustituyeron a Raphinha con Brasil porque notó unas molestias y veremos el alcance de esta lesión".

articles.title: Lamine Yamal explota el éxtasis en un minuto para la historia: 70 segundos, 25 pases, Croacia ni la toca...
articles.standfirst: Gol de España en su primer llegada sin que Croacia tocara la pelota
articles.summary: Gol de España en su primer llegada sin que Croacia tocara la pelota
articles.body: En Wembley tardó dos minutos España en marcar como campeona del mundo. En Sevilla, en su estreno en casa con la segunda estrella, solo uno. La firma fue la misma, la de Lamine Yamal. En un ambiente enloquecido, electrizante y convertido en éxtais cuando apareció Jesús Navas con la copa del mundo, la primera llegada de España al área de Livakovic fue para marcar. Sin que antes Croacia fuese capaz de entrar en contacto con la pelota. Sólo necesitó España 70 segundos para convertir Nervión en un manicomios. Con 25 pases y después un remate al primer toque de Lamine la explosión fue monumenta. Y cerca estuvo de reventar cuando jun minutos después cuando Baena tuvo el 2-0, pero lo evitó Livakovic. Ese era el gol número nueve de Lamine Yamal con la selección. Es la segunda vez que marca en dos partidos seguidos. La anterior fue ante Países Bajos, en Mestalla, en la vuelta de los cuartos de final de la Nations 2024-25, y los dos que le marcó a Francia en Stuttgart en la semifinal de junio. De esas nueve dianas que acumula el 19 de España, este queda para la historia por el valor sentimental que tiene. Y por la obra de arte con la que la selección se sumó a la fiesta en la que ya, desde antes de empezar el partido, se había convertido el estadio del Sevilla. Y de esos nueve goles de Lamine Yamal desde que debutara en septiembre de 2023 con España, son ya tres los que ha marcado antes de que el partido llegara al minuto cinco: ante Chipre en Limassol, en Wembley el pasado sábado y en Sevilla. Con el foco en Lamine Yamal por ser el ejecutor final de la obra, el tanto fue el reflejo de la manera de jugar de un equipo que es capaz de generar peligro de maneras muy distintas. Y que tiene en su banda izquierda a un jugador de una dimensión que nunca antes había conocido. Y de ese jugador que hace cosas que otros no hacen llegó el tercer gol de España. En otra acción de brillo colectivo, con un gran pase de Pedri e inteligencia de Pubill para dejar pasar la pelota, se quedó Lamine Yamal solo ante Livakovic. El meta croata dudó entre ir a tapar el remate o el pase. Y se vio con la pelota en sus redes, entrando por su palo. Poco después, a los 68 minutos, Lamine Yamal dejó el campo. La ovacón fue monumental. Se la había ganado.

articles.standfirst: Respeto absoluto del público a la leyenda croata.
articles.summary: Respeto absoluto del público a la leyenda croata.
articles.body: Atronador, vibrante, estimulante y conmovedor. El homenaje que el público del Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán hizo a Luka Modric en cada uno de los momentos que tuvo la oportunidad permanecerá para siempre en el recuerdo del centrocampista. El primer guiño llegó cuando su nombre se anunció por el videomarcador y anticipó lo que luego vendría. La ovación a Luka fue cerrada, pero menos sonora que cuando salió a calentar. En ese momento, el croata correspondió al cariño del público con aplausos y dedicándoles una sonrisa. La traca final llegó en el minuto 80. Cuando Bilic lo introdujo en el terreno de juego. Gran parte del estadio se puso en pie, lo aplaudió y coreó su nombre. El de una leyenda que 41 años que sigue jugando al fútbol con la ambición de un principiante. En España, sus 13 temporadas en el Real Madrid y el respeto con el que siempre ha tratado a todos, le ha servido para cosechar un cariño que ahora que, afronta el tramo final de su carrera, empieza a recoger. Modric es una leyenda absoluta de su país. El pasado Mundial alcanzó los 200 partidos defendiendo la camiseta de su selección y sólo Cristiano y Messi le superan en internacionalidades, aunque al argentino está a punto de atraparlo. Ha liderado la época dorada de Croacia siendo subcampeón del mundo en 2018 y tercero en Catar 2022. Registros que no hacen más que confirmar la espectacular carrera deportiva del croata. articles.title: Gordon y Kane iluminan a los 'Three Lions' en Praga
articles.standfirst: La selección inglesa completa un encuentro muy completo ante República Checa y suma los tres primeros puntos de la Nations League
articles.summary: La selección inglesa completa un encuentro muy completo ante República Checa y suma los tres primeros puntos de la Nations League
articles.body: Inglaterra llegaba a Praga con la obligación de sacar los tres puntos tras la derrota en Wembley ante España (2-3). Un encuentro en el que se mediría ante la República Checa de Santi Denia que también venía de perder ante Croacia (1-2). Vería muy pronto Sulc la tarjeta roja (en el minuto 22) en un dura entrada sobre Elliott Anderson. Aún así, el conjunto inglés no pudo marcar en la primera mitad... pero sí lo haría en el arranque de la segunda con el cabezazo de Gordon para poner el 0-1. No tardaría mucho en aparecer Harry Kane, que puso el segundo tanto con un disparo con la izquierda. Comenzó mejor Inglaterra con un gran control del esférico en Praga. Aunque la primera ocasión de peligro sería para República Checa en las botas de Sulc en un fallo de Anderson en un toque anterior. Un conjunto checo que siguió apretando y tuvo otra buena jugada tras un golpeo lejano de Cerv que no se fue muy desviado de la portería inglesa. Intentó reaccionar el conjunto inglés y lo hizo con el golpeo al palo de Morgan Rogers. Dio la sensación que los checos podían generar peligro sin hacer grandes esfuerzos. Aguantaban atrás bien replegados y salían rápido a las contras buscando la fragilidad defensiva de los Three Lions... hasta que Sulc vio la roja directa en una dura entrada con los tacos sobre la pierna de Anderson y dejaría con 10 a sus compañeros durante más de 60 minutos... La dinámica a partir de este momento sería muy similar: Inglaterra tocaba y tocaba, mientras que los checos esperaban atrás a verlas venir. Lo intentó Gordon con un golpeo con la izquierda, pero que atrapó Kovar sin mucha complicación. Vio Lewis-Skelly la primera amarilla para Inglaterra por un pisotón sobre Cerv. Se lesionó también Karabec y tuvo que entrar Lingr. Acabó la primera mitad sin que los ingleses generaran peligro claro en el área rival. Tuchel movió el banquillo al descanso e introdujo a Eze por el amonestado Lewis-Skelly buscando más pólvora arriba. De hecho, tardaría dos minutos Inglaterra en adelantarse con el cabezazo de Gordon y ya podía respirar tranquilo. Muy cerca estuvo de marcar el segundo con el disparo mordido de Lewis Hall que se fue muy cerca de la portería de Kovar. El guion del partido no cambiaría demasiado con un control total de Inglaterra del esférico en todas las partes del campo. Casi se marcaría Krejci en propia con un toque que se fue al palo. Intentaron los checos reaccionar, pero no parecía que tuvieran los recursos necesarios para ello... incluso llegó el segundo de Inglaterra con un disparo con la izquierda de Harry Kane. Tuchel quiso dar descanso a algunos de los titulares (Kane, Saka y Anderson) e introdujo a Scott, Ngumoha... y Bellingham que arrancó desde el banquillo. Probó Ambros desde fuera del área el disparo, pero estuvo atento Trafford para atajar el disparo. Salió también Gordon (el mejor jugador del partido) por Gibbs White en el 81' y el encuentro acabó con una Inglaterra muy superior.

articles.title: El embrujo de la casa del Sevilla se hace más poderoso
articles.standfirst: 28 partidos de España en los estadios del equipo de Nervión y ni una sola derrota
articles.summary: 28 partidos de España en los estadios del equipo de Nervión y ni una sola derrota
articles.body: La selección española eligió el estadio del Sevilla para jugar por primera vez en casa con las dos estrellas en la camiseta. La elección fue antes de ser campeona del mundo, a finales de junio. Se elegía una zona de seguridad, un campo talismán. Porque cuando es el Sevilla el que abre sus puertas a la selección no hay rival que sea capaz de irse con la victoria. Ocurre desde 1923, cuando España ganó 3-0 da Portugal, con los tres goles de Zabala. Era el primer español en marcar tres goles en un solo partido. A partir de ahí, un partido en el viejo Nervión y veintiséis en el actual estadio del Sevilla. Y nunca nadie fue capaz de vencerla. Croacia, tampoco. En un ambiente tremendo desde antes del partido y enloquecido desde que Lamine Yamal marcó al minuto de partido, la selección española alargó el embrujo de un estadio cargado de recuerdos y de alegrías. El partido ante los croatas quedará en el recuerdo por la fiesta vivida. Por las vibraciones y la conexión entre la grada y los jugadores. El homenaje a aquella tarde de 1964 en la que se ganó 5-1 a Irlanda y el campo del Sevilla fue una olla a presión de tal potencia que se ganó lo de ser el Jugador número 12. O la noche de 1993 e n la que se ganó a Dinamarca con el gol de Hierro para ir al Mundial de Estados Unidos. La victoria en el Sánchez-Pizjuán vale para que España alargue también las rachas asombrosas. La de 41 partidos de competición oficial seguidos sin derrotas, 40 si se mete de por medio todo lo jugado desde la derrota ante Colombia en el amistoso de Londres de marzo de 2024. Y para que Fabián Ruiz cuente sus 52 partidos con España sin derrotas. Lo que parecía imposible de igualar, los 57 de Carlos Marchena y el mejor registro mundial, entra en la cuenta atrás. A las 22.36 se pitaba el final del partido. La fiesta llegaba a su fin. Pero a los campeones del mundo les esperaba una despedida a la par de lo que se había vivido. El 4-1 era un excelente colofón. De cierre, la vuelta al campo de los campeones para agradecer una noche espectacular. El sábado, en Oviedo, les espera otra.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane full of praise for teammate and fellow Ballon d’Or contender Michael Olise
articles.summary: Michael Olise has had the most scintillating start to the season of any winger, and Harry Kane gives him his props.
articles.body:
Name a better attacking duo in world football than Michael Olise and Harry Kane .

Hey, it's been a while… no answer? Yeah, thought so.

Harry Kane is the current Ballon d'Or favourite for the 2025/26 season, while Michael Olise has had the best start of any player in the 2026/27 season, with 12 goal contributions (!!!) already in just 7 games ( Transfermarkt ). The winger has started his campaign in the best way possible and is already getting early shouts for the Ballon d'Or next year.

Harry Kane has been sensational for Bayern Munich since he joined 3 seasons ago and feels lucky to be playing with the superstar RW. In a recent interview with Bild (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), the English striker waxes lyrical of Olise. "He has made an incredible start to the season. I already thought he was fantastic last year. He had a great World Cup and has continued seamlessly from there. I believe that, thanks to his age and his mentality, he will continue to improve," stated Kane, with confidence.

Olise might have had the best 2025/26 campaign of any winger: Champions League semi-finalist with some tremendous big-game moments, World Cup single campaign assist record holder with 7 assists in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal Champion… that is one hell of a résumé for a single season.

Kane added that "The players around him motivate him, and of course, so does the coach. He is in an excellent environment to improve and continue developing. Since the start of the season, he has raised his level significantly once again." Amen.

Olise is looking unstoppable, fresh off of a hat trick against Union Berlin , which also saw him register an assist, and receive a spotless 10/10 rating from Sofascore (the only player this season to already have 2 perfect games, one against Berlin and the other against Bodø/Glimt in the Champions League).

"We need him because he is an important player for us. It was great to see him smiling after scoring his first hat-trick. I think he was proud of it – and rightly so. I really enjoy playing alongside Michael, and I also appreciate him as a person. We get along extremely well off the pitch, too," concluded Harry Kane.

Strength to strength. Olise keeps getting better.

Is this the greatest peak of any winger not named Ronaldo or Messi in football history?

Time will tell… a Champions League trophy could be exactly what the doctor prescribed.

articles.body:
COLLEGE PARK, Md. (AP) — The end of September is often when hope is peaking for Maryland football .

That's not the case this year, which is a big reason why Michael Locksley's days as coach could be numbered.

Locksley was already in the hot-seat discussion before the season started, and after two straight losses to teams with new coaches — Virginia Tech and UCLA — the Terrapins are reeling at a time when they were supposed to be making progress . Last weekend's Big Ten opener at home was a 54-3 shellacking by the Bruins, the type of defeat that can put a coach past the point of no return with his bosses.

Still, Monday's weekly meeting between Locksley and athletic director Jim Smith apparently came and went without much drama. At least, that's what the coach said at his Tuesday news conference previewing Saturday's matchup at Nebraska .

"It was a typical weekly meeting where we discussed the program, where it is," Locksley said. "It was a standard meeting, personnel matters like we always talk about."

Locksley was asked if he's been assured of anything regarding his status.

"My focus has been on getting us ready to play up at Lincoln," he said. "No need for assurances."

Locksley is in his eighth season as Maryland 's coach, not counting a stint as interim coach back in 2015. His first full season in charge was 2019, and the Terrapins did have a stretch from 2021-23 in which they won three straight bowl games, which they'd never done.

Since then, though, the decline has been significant. Maryland went 4-8 in 2024. The Terps then started 4-0 last year behind freshman quarterback Malik Washington , but they blew a big fourth-quarter lead at home against Washington, then a smaller one at home against Nebraska. Maryland would not win another game that season.

The Terps have now dropped 17 of their last 19 Big Ten games. For a while, Maryland at least could point to a lengthy winning streak in nonconference games, but that 20-game run ended when former Terrapins assistant James Franklin came in with his Virginia Tech team and thumped the Terps two weekends ago.

Then Washington threw four interceptions against UCLA, and that game turned into a total debacle for the Terrapins. Now a program that's become known for starting fast and fading must try to do the opposite.

With teams increasingly willing to fire coaches during the season, every game feels crucial for Locksley.

"To address the fans, I understand the frustration our fans have. They care and expect to win, just like we do," Locksley said. "I know our team is disappointed in the way they've played the last couple of games. But just like I expect, just like I've modeled for them, we know that the only way to get it fixed is to play better."

This week's trip to Nebraska is no easy task. The following week's game at Ohio State figures to be even harder. Can Locksley survive as coach until the Oct. 17 home game against Rutgers? Would winning that one even matter, with the open date afterward providing a natural break in the schedule that could offer time to regroup after a coaching change?

Locksley certainly seems aware of all the talk about his future, even if he tries to avoid it when possible.

"I'm 56 years old," he said. "I know how to insulate myself. I know how to put my phone down. I know how to not read or indulge with things that aren't going to help prepare the team for the next opponent, which is Nebraska. What I've tried to do is model that for some of our players. I know that they are bombarded by a lot of the things that go on outside of the building."

articles.title: Big Ten rival should 'try to pry' one of Indiana football coordinators, analyst says
articles.summary: A league rival should try to poach one of Curt Cignetti's coordinators, one analyst suggests, if their head coach gets fired.
articles.body:
Mike Shanahan and Bryant Haines have been faithful assistants for Indiana football coach Curt Cignetti .

Shanahan, the offensive coordinator, is in his fifth season working with Cignetti. James Madison had a 19-4 record in 2022-23, and he followed Cignetti to IU, which is 31-2 with a national championship over 2+ seasons. Last year's team featured Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Fernando Mendoza .

Haines, the defensive coordinator, won the Broyles Award as last season's best assistant coach after the Hoosiers ranked in the top five nationally in rushing, scoring and total defense on the way to the national title. His association with Cignetti dates to their Division II days at Indiana of Pennsylvania , and he is in his sixth season as a coordinator for Cignetti.

Cignetti is aware both have head coaching aspirations, and teams may call in the coming offseason. An early possibility is Maryland , according to Sports Illustrated's Pat Forde . The Terrapins (2-2) are coming off a 54-3 loss to UCLA and have finished with a winning record in three of coach Mike Locksley's eight full seasons.

Forde contends either could probably retain some Washington, D.C., area talent and better contend in the Big Ten.

" Maryland should probably try to pry one of the coordinators off Indiana 's staff," Forde wrote this week. "Both OC Mike Shanahan and DC Bryant Haines were on Cignetti's staff from 2019 to '23 at James Madison , where they dramatically out-recruited everyone in the DMV area when it came to identifying underrated prospects. When trying to lift up a losing program in the Big Ten, Cignetti stands as the beacon of hope and imitation."

articles.title: New coach, new players, but same old failings hamper Scotland
articles.summary: Self-inflicted wounds cost Scotland on Sebastien Pocognoli's Hampden debut, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
Scotland fans came to Hampden to welcome the new man, Sebastien Pocognoli, and left with all the woes of old weighing them down as they went.

More calamitous defending in the beginning, another self-inflicted wound that was a complete game-changer, another day without a goal - four in a row now.

In the early minutes when Jack Hendry got himself sent off, we may as well have been back amid the meltdown of Miami. Then, Scotland gifted Brazil one goal and then two when they made a fiendishly-difficult job an impossible one on the back of slapstick in defence.

So it was again on Tuesday. Hendry's red card was a grim moment that sucked the life out of the occasion.

Switzerland don't lose many games. Argentina had the devil's own job in seeing them off in extra-time at the World Cup. Germany beat them 4-3 in a friendly, the winner only coming in the 85th minute.

They're full of nous and strength and belief. Their coach, Murat Yakin, has the calm authority of a man who knows, with absolute certainty, that his team will prevail.

Once the opening goal went in, Yakin turned around in his technical area with a half-smile on his face. Job done, already.

Pocognoli still awaits first goal after 10-man Scotland lose to Switzerland

Who 'battled impressively' for Scots? And how did you rate players?

Hampden debut to forget but Pocognoli looks at bigger picture

There was little Scotland could do about the brilliant way the Swiss cut them open to send Dan Ndoye away so early in the game, but there was plenty Hendry could have done - or should not have done - when he was at the heart of a foot-rush and a mismatch. Watching it unfold was painful.

Ndoye was always winning the race. An experienced defender, Hendry knew that. He also would have known that any desperate and ill-fated attempt to halt Ndoye was only going to end one way.

He was in no position to make a legitimate challenge. He needed to accept his fate and hope against hope that his goalkeeper was going to save him.

Of the unpleasant options, he picked the one he could not pick. Reaching out to grab Ndoye was a fatal act.

Later, captain Andy Robertson tried to explain what might have been going through Hendry's head, saying that it is anathema to a defender to just allow a striker a shot on goal, that every fibre of their being tells them to do something to stop it.

Hindsight is lovely, he said. "Football is about split-second decisions ... but the red card killed us."

Off Hendry went, in went the free-kick, and Scotland were a goal behind and a man down against the 14th best team in the world.

Could Angus Gunn have done better with Ricardo Rodriguez's effort? Yes, it flew in on the goalkeeper's side of the wall and he didn't lay a glove on it. A nightmarish beginning.

Hendry's night ended woefully early and so did Kieron Bowie's, the striker substituted in the wake of the red, an innocent victim of a dreadful error.

Scotland worked like dervishes in the aftermath. They fought and scraped. John McGinn bought a bunch of fouls; Oli McBurnie battled hard in what McGinn called a "thankless task"; there were some fleeting moments when the crowd got energised and hope, or perhaps delusion, took hold.

Pocognoli's underdogs tried to stay in the game, but there was an inevitability about it all. Switzerland dealt handily with Scotland's enthusiasm and waited to land the knockout blows, which came later on.

A second goal didn't flatter them. Neither did a third. This was always going to be a huge ask when it was 11 v 11. When it became 10 v 11 in 11 minutes, the night was effectively over.

That's the galling thing. Maybe it would have ended the same way if the red had never happened, but we never got the chance to find out.

Pocognoli said that everybody in the squad was "so excited to start the first page of the book at home", but the book turned into a horror story.

The next chapter comes in Skopje on Saturday. You hesitate to call it a must-win so soon in Pocognoli's reign, but for feel-good purposes it really is.

North Macedonia are no Switzerland, who beat them 3-0 last weekend. They're not even at Slovenia's level, having lost 2-0 to them on Tuesday.

They are winless in 10 games, have scored two goals in that time and shipped four against Turkey, four against Denmark and seven against Wales.

This is a game when the Scotland goal drought needs to end and the run of games without a win needs to be brought to be an abrupt conclusion.

What Pocognoli does with his line-up and formation will be debated heavily because the 90 minutes against Switzerland really told us nothing. Or almost nothing.

Luis Binks defended well on his debut and Stephen Welsh came on after the red card and performed admirably again. Plus marks on an otherwise non-entity of a night.

Bowie was robbed of his evening and will surely be given a proper chance in Skopje. That McBurnie-Bowie combination deserves an opportunity to prove its worth having been broken up so prematurely at Hampden.

Needing goals and pace and unpredictability, the manager might see this as a time for Ben Gannon-Doak, a tough customer to get into his system, but a speedster who is worth the effort in figuring out how to do it.

You could see the logic of him not playing wing-back against the accomplished Swiss, but no such threat exists against North Macedonia.

Not scoring against Slovenia was annoying; not scoring against Switzerland - in the circumstances - was understandable; not scoring and winning in Skopje would be a horrible outcome.

Time to cut loose - or what constitutes cutting loose for a team that has lost their ability to score. The Scott McTominay overhead kick, the Kieran Tierney wonder goal, the Kenny McLean shot from the other end of the world seem like an awfully long time ago now.

You pine for an ugly deflection, a madcap own goal, one that ricochets in off McGinn's backside or the back of McBurnie's head. Anything for a goal and a win. Anything.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Hints at QB1 Decision Between Julian Lewis, Isaac Wilson for Colorado vs. Texas Tech
articles.summary: Colorado head coach Deion Sanders didn't commit to a starting quarterback between Julian Lewis and Isaac Wilson for the upcoming game against Texas Tech, but he may have hinted at the answer Tuesday.
articles.body:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders didn't commit to a starting quarterback between Julian Lewis and Isaac Wilson for the upcoming game against Texas Tech, but he may have hinted at the answer Tuesday.

"I haven't talked to JuJu," Sanders told reporters . "I talked to Isaac. The kid is excited about the possibilities. … He stood up in a meeting and really talked to the team about this and that challenged them in many ways. So I'm proud of that young man. I really am."

Lewis started the first four games of the season but was replaced by Wilson during Saturday's loss to Baylor.

Wilson provided a spark and went 12-of-25 for 156 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions, although it wasn't enough in the 23-13 defeat. His touchdown pass in the fourth quarter tied the game, but the Bears scored the final 10 points to give the Buffaloes a second straight loss.

It was also a disappointing development for Lewis after he struggled during the 41-7 blowout loss to Northwestern the previous game.

He was 19-of-29 for 168 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions against the Wildcats in a defeat that ended any momentum on Colorado's side following season-opening wins over Georgia Tech and Weber State.

There was no shortage of expectations surrounding Lewis as a highly regarded 4-star prospect in the recruiting class of 2025, per 247Sports .

He started last season behind Kaidon Salter but combined for three touchdown passes and zero interceptions in two late-season games against West Virginia and Arizona State. With that as the backdrop, it was reasonable to expect Lewis to take a leap in 2026.

However, it hasn't happened yet, and his starting role could be in jeopardy.

articles.title: USMNT vs. Chile Score, Highlights, Stats and Reaction
articles.summary: Make it two promising performances in a row from the USMNT.
articles.body:
Make it two promising performances in a row from the USMNT.

The Americans defeated Chile 4-2 on Tuesday night, their second straight victory over a South American opponent in their first friendlies since this summer's World Cup.

Sebastian Berhalter, Julian Hall, Chris Richards and Mathis Albert all scored for the USMNT.

Diego Ulloa and Maximiliano Gutiérrez each found the back of the net for Chile.

There was also a heated confrontation between the teams late in the contest:

It was Hall's second straight game with a goal for the USMNT after he also tallied in last Wednesday's 4-1 win over Peru.

The youth movement has been real for the USMNT over the past two contests. Hall was one of two teenagers to score on Wednesday, joining Justin Ellis. Star prospect Cavan Sullivan made appearances in both fixtures. Eight teenagers made their debut appearance on Tuesday as Mauricio Pochettino keeps his eyes fixed on the future of the program.

But beyond just the youngsters, there was plenty to like about Tuesday's performance, including Berhalter continuing to state his case for a bigger role:

The USMNT finished the contest dominating possession (58 percent) and had more shots on target (8-7), though Chile out-shot the United States (14-13) and had a stark advantage in corners (13-5).

Up next for the United States is a matchup against rivals Mexico (Saturday, Oct. 3) and Canada (Tuesday, Oct. 6) during the extended international break.

articles.title: Young U.S. men's soccer team has ups and downs in 4-2 victory over Chile
articles.summary: But all in all, it was another good result and fun outing for a program returning from the World Cup with the second of four friendlies over 11 days.
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS — Amid all the excitement about his young U.S. soccer team, a wide-eyed crew that started the new World Cup cycle with an enlightening performance over the weekend , Mauricio Pochettino warned there would be ups and downs along the way.

After all, almost half the roster had never played at the senior level and, as a whole, the group hadn't spent much time together.

Tuesday's 4-2 victory over Chile at bubbly Energizer Park reinforced the coach's admonition.

The gorgeous build-up on the first goal.

Sebastian Berhalter and Gio Reyna putting their stamp on another match.

Teenager Julian Hall 's second goal in two appearances, and teenager Mathis Albert scoring his first. At 17 years and 4 months, Albert is the youngest scorer in U.S. history.

Chris Richards ' 72nd-minute tiebreaking goal as part of a second-half comeback.

All in all, it was another good result and fun outing for a program returning from the World Cup with the second of four friendlies over 11 days. For the second time in four days, the Americans scored four goals and flexed their muscles against a South American foe.

There were troubling moments, as well, particularly in the first half, when the Americans conceded numerous scoring opportunities and made many mistakes. They were fortunate to be tied at intermission.

But they showed resilience in the second half and, coupled with the 4-1 thumping of Peru last Saturday in Orlando , continued building momentum heading into this Saturday's showdown with rival Mexico in greater Phoenix. They will also play Canada on Oct. 6 in St. Paul, Minnesota.

In a pregame ceremony in his hometown, World Cup captain Tim Ream was honored for 16 years and 86 appearances with the national team. The Charlotte FC center back, who will turn 39 on Friday, announced moments earlier that he has retired from international soccer and won't weigh his club future until after the MLS season.

"The kids are getting younger and younger," he said. Ream was talking about the U.S. roster, not his own three kids.

"I actually got a text message last night [that] I was a senior at Saint Louis University when [17-year-old forward Cavan Sullivan ] was born," Ream said. "I was like, 'He's only four years older than my oldest.'"

Ream was not selected to the current roster.

The starting lineup Tuesday averaged just over 23 years old, including teenagers Hall, Neil Pierre and Adri Mehmeti . The other young starters were midfielder Brooklyn Raines , 21, and right back Frankie Westfield, 20.

At almost 6-foot-7, the 18-year-old Pierre was unmistakable on the backline. Like Sullivan, he is enjoying a breakout club campaign with the Philadelphia Union .

Reyna was the only holdover starter from the Peru match. Like Saturday, Pochettino started six 2026 World Cup players: Reyna, Berhalter, goalkeeper Chris Brady , wingers Antonee Robinson and Sergiño Dest, and center back Miles Robinson .

Brady, 22, made his first international start after debuting as a sub in a World Cup tuneup.

Chile — which has missed three World Cups since winning the 2016 Copa America — was without captain Gabriel Suazo and Lucas Cepeda , La Liga-based players red-carded in the 1-0 loss to Canada on Saturday in Toronto.

As they did against Peru, the Americans threatened early off a Reyna set piece. His free kick from 25 yards met Miles Robinson for a point-blank header that Lawrence Vigouroux slapped aside in spectacular fashion.

The U.S. was organized and energetic at the start but not always precise. In the 18th minute, a miscommunication between Berhalter and Mehmeti led to a Chilean threat. A minute later, Berhalter's tasty through ball sent Hall in alone, but after rounding Vigouroux, his off-balance, angled bid missed high and wide.

Brady was shaky, sitting back when he should've come forward and allowing Victor Méndez to test him. Then, on shots a minute apart, he also got lucky as Ben Brereton 's screamer dinged the crossbar and Darío Osorio 's low bid hit the far post.

Against the run of play, the match took an unforeseen turn.

Two minutes after Osorio's scare, the Americans went ahead in the 37th on a wonderfully constructed goal. They won the ball in midfield. Dest and Reyna played a sharp combination. With quick and clever footwork, Dest danced into the box. He crossed to Hall, who dummied the ball with the smarts of a veteran, allowing Berhalter to bury a 12-yarder into the far post.

Brady's problems continued. On the last act of the half — a Chilean corner kick — he punched the ball up, then backward. A mad scramble ensued. Finally, from inside the six-yard box, Diego Ulloa's side-volley caromed off Westfield's arm and into the net.

Brady's night — or nightmare — was over. As he did against Peru, Pochettino changed his goalkeeper at halftime: FC Cincinnati 's Brian Schwake made his first appearance, becoming the 12th debut in this camp.

He couldn't do much about Maxi Gutiérrez's go-ahead goal in the 49th minute. Westfield's misstruck header in midfield allowed Gutiérrez to glide into the U.S. end. Berhalter failed to shut him down, and the Chilean forward whistled a 23-yard shot into the far corner with pinpoint accuracy.

Two minutes later, the U.S. answered. Reyna lifted a gentle cross into the box, where Hall rose from eight yards and headed it into the far side.

Pochettino turned to his bench and made seven subs, including five veterans. Vigouroux made a fine foot save on Antonee Robinson, but on the ensuing corner kick, Berhalter delivered a perfect ball to Richards for a powerful header from the edge of the six-yard box.

Chile threatened to pull even. The U.S. extended the lead on Albert's stab off the underside of the crossbar from close range. The announced crowd of 21,680 loved it.

Just before the final whistle, a benches-emptying scuffle broke out after a Chilean player tapped the fallen Schwake on the arm with his foot. Play resumed, but at the final whistle, another brief incident broke out.

"Take Me Home, Country Roads" boomed over the speakers.

Winger Cole Campbell, a first-time camper held out of the Peru match for an undisclosed ailment, and goalkeeper Diego Kochen , who played the second half Saturday, were not in uniform. Kochen was healthy, but Pochettino chose to dress 26 players again.

In his 60th appearance, Antonee Robinson captained the team for the first time.

Sullivan replaced Berhalter in the 83rd minute.

The Americans are 11-1-3 in greater St. Louis, including 5-0-0 at Energizer Park, which sits 1.3 miles directly west of the Gateway Arch and opened before the 2023 MLS season.

articles.title: El 'Virus FIFA' deja 'huérfanos' a casi el 75% de los equipos de Segunda
articles.standfirst: 16 de los 22 perderán a algún jugador al menos un partido • Afecta una temporada más a una Liga que se resiste a detenerse • El Girona, con seis futbolistas, el más afectado
articles.summary: El parón de selecciones se lleva jugadores en 16 de los 22 • Afecta una temporada más a una Segunda que se resiste a detenerse • El Girona, con seis futbolistas, es el más afectado
articles.body: Como cada temporada, el famoso Virus FIFA se digiere con especial resignación e incredulidad en la Segunda división española. Se trata de la única categoría de plata de las grandes Ligas europeas que no unifica su calendario con el de la máxima categoría y que, por lo tanto, no se detiene durante los compromisos de selecciones. Los clubes afrontan su segunda semana de trabajo sin varios de sus futbolistas internacionales, una situación que hace tiempo que dejó de ser una simple anécdota para convertirse en un auténtico problema para la mayoría de los equipos. Durante este parón de septiembre y octubre, hasta 34 futbolistas se van a perder al menos un partido de LaLiga Hypermotion por la llamada de sus respectivas selecciones, una circunstancia que afecta de forma directa a 16 de los 22 clubes que integran la categoría de plata. Es decir, casi el 73% de los equipos se han visto perjudicados por la convocatoria de, al menos, un jugador. Tan sólo Eibar, Sabadell, Oviedo, Sporting, Real Sociedad B y Albacete se han mantenido al margen de este virus internacional. Para más inri, la mayoría de estos futbolistas no sólo se perderán una jornada, sino dos, ya que el parón se prolongará, en la mayoría de los casos, hasta el próximo 7 de octubre. El caso más llamativo lo protagoniza esta vez el Girona, que perdió hasta seis jugadores en la pasada jornada y volverá a quedarse sin varios de ellos en el exigente duelo del domingo contra el Mallorca, otro de los grandes perjudicados, con tres internacionales ausentes. Resulta curioso, además, que algunos de los encuentros más atractivos de la competición coincidan precisamente con las ventanas FIFA, cuando la Primera división detiene su actividad. En la Jornada 7 ya se disputó un Mallorca-Almería con cinco bajas por compromisos internacionales entre ambos equipos. En el caso de los indálicos, además, con dos titulares indiscutibles como Dzodic y Cipenga. A ello se sumó el siempre atractivo derbi asturiano Oviedo-Sporting. Y este próximo fin de semana llegará otro de los grandes partidos del campeonato, el Girona-Mallorca, nuevamente condicionado por numerosas ausencias. Luis García, técnico del Mallorca, fue un paso más allá en la previa del pasado encuentro frente al Almería al referirse a esta coincidencia en el calendario. En tono irónico, deslizó que confía "mucho en que ha caído de esa manera y no lo podemos elegir... no pensemos mal". Otro de los entrenadores que más ha alzado la voz en los últimos años en favor de una unificación de calendarios con la Primera división es Rubi, ex técnico del Almería, quien en la temporada 2024-25 denunció que la competición estaba "adulterada" después de tener que disputar los playoffs sin dos futbolistas tan importantes como Luis Suárez y Pubill. En definitiva, el debate vuelve a ponerse sobre la mesa cada vez que llega un parón internacional. Mientras las principales Ligas europeas sincronizan sus calendarios para proteger la igualdad competitiva, la Segunda española continúa obligando a numerosos clubes a competir en clara desventaja. Una realidad asumida por todos desde hace años, pero que sigue sin encontrar una solución y que cada temporada alimenta la sensación de que el calendario penaliza a quienes más mérito tienen por contar con futbolistas de nivel internacional.

articles.title: Este Atlético ya va lanzado a por todo
articles.standfirst: Tras un inicio con dudas, los de Simeone han alcanzado la velocidad de crucero con tres triunfos seguidos
articles.summary: Tras un inicio con dudas, los de Simeone han alcanzado la velocidad de crucero con tres triunfos seguidos
articles.body: Estamos en reconstrucción”, ha deslizado en varias ocasiones Simeone para explicar el arranque de temporada. Dos pinchazos ante Villarreal y Athletic fueron los cinco puntos que han volado en este inicio de temporada. Desde San Mamés, a volar. Tres victorias, incluido un meritorio 0-3 en Anoeta y el derbi del Metropolitano, para convertirse en la principal alternativa al implacable Barça. Así, los rojiblancos se marcharon al parón segundos, a cinco puntos de los de Flick y por encima de un Madrid al que volvieron a derrotar. Más allá de la polémica, fue un encuentro en el que cuatro de los cinco fichajes fueron titulares y rindieron a un gran nivel. Marcaron, de hecho, los dos tantos: Grimaldo y Jonathan David. Pero, sobre todo, demostraron que esta vez sí han llegado para dar un salto en el techo competitivo del Atlético, con Cuti Romero y Kang in como principales ejemplos de asentarse al poco de llegar. Nada de la mili de Simeone, como otras temporadas. El principal lunar ha sido, sin duda, la lesión de Pablo Barrios. Jugador generacional, destinado a liderar el equipo, una nueva dolencia muscular le ha sacado de un grupo en el que Sorloth no ha llegado ni a entrar. Los goles de David mitigan la ausencia del noruego, mientras la sombra del culebrón Julián sobrevuela al equipo desde hace meses. Recuperar a la Araña es, sin duda, uno de los objetivos de Simeone. Que el argentino recupere la versión de su primera temporada ayudaría a que el Atlético no pierda comba respecto al Barça. De momento, la reconstrucción va por buen camino, como demuestra las tres victorias seguidas en las que Oblak, otro de los grandes destacados, ha tenido un papel prioritario para ver a un Atlético lanzado a por todo. Seguridad defensiva. Arrancó el curso encajando ocho goles en cuatro partidos, pero en las últimas tres victorias ha encajado sólo un gol. El Cuti se ha asentado en la zaga y con él, los del Cholo han recuperado la fiabilidad atrás. San Mamés. Una derrota en siete jornadas... pero muy dolorosa. Tras una buena primera parte, los de Simeone perdieron el choque en apenas dos minutos. Dos despistes que no se han vuelto a repetir. La nota del Atlético de Madrid en esta primera fase de la temporada se queda en un 8. Notable alto para los hombres de Diego Pablo Simeone, que han conseguido enderezar el rumbo tras los malos resultados cosechados ante el Villarreal y el Athletic. La derrota en Liverpool en el estreno de la Champions entraba dentro de los escenarios posibles. Son varios los candidatos que optan ser el MVP del Atlético de Madrid. Hasta el momento reconocimiento es para Álex Baena. El almeriense sigue la buena inercia del Mundial y está siendo el jugador más destacado. Alexander Sorloth no ha tenido suerte con las lesiones y el delantero noruego aún no ha podido debutar esta temporada. El equipo ha echado de menos su presencia, sobre todo en los primeros partidos, en los que tuvo que jugar sin un delantero de referencia.

articles.standfirst: El pésimo arranque del equipo dinamitó la estructura deportiva con el despido de Corberán y del ceo de fútbol, Ron Gourlay, y sus colaboradores directos
articles.summary: El pésimo arranque del equipo dinamitó la estructura deportiva con el despido de Corberán y del ceo de fútbol, Ron Gourlay, y sus colaboradores directos
articles.body: El Valencia podía haber empezado peor la temporada. Pero es muy difícil. Por eso está viviendo este parón internacional en penúltima posición, con unos raquíticos 4 puntos, y se está tomando estas tres semanas como una mini pretemporada sobre la que tratar de enderezar su caída en barrena. Alarmado por la situación, por lo que vio en el palco contra el Barcelona (0-5), y aconsejado por el director general del club, el presidente Kiat Lim fulminó la estructura deportiva que él mismo había bendecido en Singapur un año antes. Cayó el CEO de Fútbol, Ron Gourlay, y su red de ojeadores tras un decepcionante mercado de verano; y cayó el entrenador, Carlos Corberán, del que había desconectado el núcleo duro de la plantilla. Lo cierto es que el Valencia exhibía las mismas carencias del arranque de la temporada anterior, con un agravante: una plaga de lesiones que mermaba aún más la capacidad de reacción de un equipo limitado en todos sus frentes. El técnico valenciano apostaba por una línea de cinco defensas, y por una propuesta reactiva en casi todos los partidos. Así rascó un empate contra el Celta en el primer partido de Liga disputado en Mestalla y ya. Después, perdió contra el Betis –aunque fue el partido en el que mereció mejor suerte por juego y ocasiones-. Ya se puede imaginar el lector cómo debió de ser el partido frente al Deportivo, en Riazor, cuando el entrenador -ya cuestionado y dejado caer por el vestuario- lo calificó de "vergonzoso". Entre los errores defensivos y la nula capacidad de respuesta el Valencia se entregó en una primera parte desconcertante. Tras el paseo triunfal del Barcelona en Mestalla, Corberán y Gourlay liquidaron su crédito con los cero tiros a puerta en el Pizjuán. Porque esa semana ya se habían producido movimientos para fichar a Braulio Vázquez (Osasuna), como director deportivo, y que el gallego eligiera al nuevo entrenador. El Valencia hizo su partido más potable de este arranque de Liga en Mendizorroza, con un solo entrenamiento de Óscar Sánchez como técnico interino que firmó la única victoria del equipo pro el momento. Una muestra más de que lo que se había roto en el vestuario era imposible de recomponer mientras siguiera Corberán. Los datos son apabullantes: cuatro puntos de 21, cuatro goles a favor y 13 en contra. Y lo que no se ve en los datos. Una carestía competitiva que permitió que le volara un punto en Mestalla en el tiempo añadido contra la Real. Javier Aguirre desembarcó en Paterna el jueves 24 de septiembre. Por lo pronto, le ha cambiado la cara al equipo en los entrenamientos. Ahora tiene que conseguir el mismo efecto en los partidos. No era fácil quedarse con una sola decepción. Pero la mayor de todas ha sido el técnico. Tras salvar al Valencia de un descenso casi seguro en la segunda vuelta de la temporada 2023-24, el técnico fue dilapidando su crédito desde la misma foto con Ron Gourlay en Singapur. La estructura deportiva lo ponía a él en el centro de la planificación deportiva, mientras iba perdiendo autoridad en el vestuario. Entre las otras decepciones de la plantilla se podría señalar a Dieng -fichaje de este verano-, Tárrega -que ha perdido la contundencia que mostraba temporadas atrás- o Ugrinic, que no ha dado el paso adelante que se esperaba. Es el mejor que representa el paso adelante de la cantera. No ha marcado ningún gol -como Aarón Mayol-, aunque ha sido el más constante en ofrecer alternativas desde que Corberán lo hizo jugar en la segunda parte ante el Deportivo. Tiene muchas cosas que pulir aún, seguro, pero puede marcar diferencias. Entre los jugadores que evitan la quema en este arranque de curso -con minutos de juego- se podrían añadir a Javi Guerra o Danjuma. Han mostrado su calidad, pero con cuentagotas. La irrupción de Mayol, Otorbi y Aimar Blázquez -aunque solo fueron unos minutos- muestra que hay recursos que pueden dar un paso adelante, aunque no sea el mejor contexto para desarrollar su talento. No es muy buena señal que el club haya despedido a toda la estructura deportiva 12 días después del cierre de mercado. Las carencias de la plantilla (central y delantero) habrá que resolverlas en invierno.

articles.title: ‘Every time they speak, they attack Barcelona’ – Joan Laporta takes aim at Real Madrid
articles.summary: Relations between the two clubs are very frosty indeed.
articles.body:
Barcelona president Joan Laporta has taken aim at Real Madrid once again and has spoken out after a date was set for the two clubs to meet in court.

The Catalans have threatened legal action against Florentino Perez following his comments made earlier this year, and Laporta says the club had no choice but to take action.

"What we cannot accept is the distortion of the truth, and that every time they speak publicly, they attack Barça. Our legal department reacts to these situations. We do so with everyone who has condemned us before we've even been tried and has said things that weren't true, and we continue in the same vein," he told Mundo Deportivo.

"What I hope is that they rectify this and that it gets resolved. As you know, relations with Real Madrid have broken down.

"They appeared in the Negreira case, which we understand was only to prolong the case and justify their television channel's actions and a predetermined narrative. And that's where the conflict lies, and the existing relationship is nonexistent."

The two clubs are now due to meet in a court in Madrid on November 25th for a conciliation hearing, with Barca willing to file a complaint if Perez does not retract his comments.

articles.title: Can Sunderland Crack Open 12-Year-Old Champagne?
articles.summary: Manchester City’s long-running financial investigation could have unexpected consequences for Sunderland - but would we really want the 2014 League Cup hande...
articles.body:
The long-running investigation into Manchester City 's finances is far from breaking news, but before the weekend it was reported that it is likely that the Etihad outfit will be found guilty of most of the 115 charges levied against them. The news had been leaked and then last night confirmed, but as yet there is still no decision on what the punishment will be for the mega-rich Blues for the period in question, 2009-18.

For all the time that the investigation has gone on – and we are talking years here – like most other Sunderland fans, I only followed the story with a passing interest. That is until I was reading a report on Friday which listed the clubs that would benefit if City were to be stripped of the trophies they won in that period of 2009-18.

The clubs who have been mainly concerned with it all this time are the two clubs that finished as runners-up to City when they won the Premier League three times in the above-mentioned period – Manchester United , who would win two more titles to add to their collection, and Liverpool , who would gain one.

The report then listed, for our continuing passive interest, the following beneficiaries:

Which is where I, for one, stopped and did a double take.

It's not a thought that most of our fan base had ever really considered in this long-running saga. That somehow we could go back to that moment and be awarded the trophy?

There is nothing definite as yet. The only fact is that City have been found guilty, with no word as to what form the punishment will take. Stripping them of all the trophies they won in the offending period is only one possibility among many.

The same leaked sources also mentioned that there seems to be little appetite among the Premiership to strip City of their titles, but it should be pointed out that, first of all, the punishment will be decided by an independent panel and not the Premier League, and second, the EFL Cup isn't run by the Premier League, it's a Football League competition.

But in regard to the question of being awarded the 2014 EFL Cup, how do we feel about it as a fan base?

Memories of the day and game itself are a match in which our (then struggling) team came up against one of the top teams in the country and gave it a real go against them. Fabio Borini 's fabulous first-half strike took us into dream world for a while, before we were undone by an even better strike from Yaya Touré , and what you have to say was a superior team overturned us. But despite being beaten, many hold good memories of the day and of the cup run.

That was then, and twelve years later, it would seem strange to celebrate it now.

There are parallels here between this case and our promotion to the top flight following Swindon's demotion after the 1990 League Play-Off Final at Wembley – again for financial irregularities. But on that occasion, Swindon were already being measured for a noose around their neck before the game kicked off. We were notified within a short time and we did celebrate our promotion, albeit with Dennis Smith and his staff popping champagne corks on the Roker pitch.

This time, everyone from 2014, from the chairman down to the kit man, have long since departed. For the most part, the only people left at the Stadium of Light of any note are us. The fans.

We will take adding a trophy to our cabinet – and one which we have never won before. If anything, it would mean we had won it before the Visitors!

There are many that will take it because the team that beat us did it by what is perceived as cheating and an unfair means. You can say we were not beaten fair and square, and just as Swindon were stripped of their right to play in (the then) Division One, then City should hand any trophies they won over to the teams that they beat. Yet, if this happens, the opinion among our own fan base is likely to be split.

Who would take it and who would rather we won it on the pitch?

articles.title: Sunderland In The Europa League: A Chance To Make More History?
articles.summary: What kinds of hopes and expectations are we harbouring for our first European campaign in over fifty years?
articles.body:
I have a feeling that we'll do very well in the Europa League this season.

Whilst we never really know what players and staff are thinking or preparing for, sometimes it's true that when the fans are up for a game, you can bet this feeds into the attitude and passion of the players.

Although everyone trots out the expected (and valid) remark that the Premier League is the bread and butter and must be the main focus, you can't tell me that a fixture such as Crystal Palace away can match a European fixture.

All the European games will be hotly contested by the squad and everyone will want to be involved, and I would hesitate to say more so than a Premier League game. I often bang on about the importance of psychology in sport, and in my opinion, it's the Europa League adventure that lights the touch paper for most players and fans.

So with that in mind, I do believe we'll certainly qualify directly for the knockout stages and quarter-finals. After that, anything is possible.

The biggest reason for belief in Sunderland 's success in the Europa League is the simple fact that we're one of the best teams in the Europa League.

The Opta supercomputer may seem to consistently underrate us in the Premier League, but right now it has Sunderland as the twenty ninth best team in the world — that's right, the world!

That's fifth-best of all Europa League teams, behind only Benfica, Bournemouth , Royale Union Saint-Gilloise and Bayer Leverkusen . Most importantly, it's better than every squad we'll play in the Europa League group stages as Milan (47), Lech Poznan (78) and Dinamo Zagreb (82) are the only ones under 100.

That said, I don't believe it'll be easy.

AZ Alkmaar at 105 gave us all we could handle at the Stadium of Light, and AC Milan and Lech Poznan are both on the road. But back to the positives: we're simply a very good team with very good players with a ton of experience in European play.

The players have to know the Europa League is the competition Sunderland has the best chance of winning this season, and I can't believe that won't have a a positive impact on their play throughout the competition.

The only thing that stands in the way of the quarter-finals (at worst) is poor health or Premier League relegation fears.

After watching Sunderland take on AZ Alkmaar earlier this month, it clarified a feeling inside of me that Sunderland simply have to give this European campaign absolutely everything, as it's simply what the fans deserve.

The comments will always come in the media, but what about the Premier League? Can they handle two games a week? Could it prompt a relegation battle?

Forget all that. This campaign is what I've been dreaming of since I started supporting Sunderland.

The unforgettable atmospheres. Playing teams you'd never dreamed of facing. Journeys to cities and towns that would never arise as a holiday spot. For Sunderland, while I hope it happens again, there's no certainties that it will and we have to give it everything.

Beating AZ was a brilliant start and eases the pressure on the group. We have some very difficult away ties but if our home form is strong, we're very likely to qualify and I think we have to view this as a "Why not?".

Why can't we go all the way? We proved last season that we can get results at difficult grounds — Anfield, Stamford Bridge and St. James' Park to name a few, and no club will enjoy a visit to the Stadium of Light on an evening with our atmosphere.

In the summer, Sunderland added depth and if we don't face unlucky periods with injuries including Brian Brobbey and Dan Ballard , we do have two players for every position and can rotate marginally, you'd expect.

Players like Chemsdine Talbi for example, aren't even getting any league minutes at present, which shows you how much we're building in a short period of time.

My huge hope is that we don't overly prioritise the league given what a unique opportunity this season for us as fans, as like I said, why can't we go deep into the competition and maybe, maybe just head to Frankfurt come May?

Embarking on a Europa League campaign marks a step into the unknown for Sunderland.

After years of futility and of watching the likes of Newcastle and Middlesbrough enjoy countless memorable European nights, we've been given key card access to a very exclusive members' lounge with panoramic views, high-definition TVs and a fully stocked minibar (Password in case of a lost key: "RégisLeBrisIsGod").

With that in mind, I suppose the issue is whether we're here to flirt with this competition in a brief yet glorious manner or whether we've already gotten a taste for it and are determined to challenge as strongly as we can.

My own belief is simple: we do have the players to make a real impact in this competition and in Régis Le Bris, we have a coach that'll relish the challenges posed by continental sides at home and away, but it's going to be the trickiest of balancing acts to ensure that we can remain competitive in the Premier League and retain genuine hopes of at least reaching the knockout stages of the Europa League.

The games will come thick and fast; rotation will occasionally be needed and we'll be placing fairly sizable demands on our fringe players to see games through, but this is life at this level. You have to find solutions and ways to deal with a packed schedule whilst never forgetting the fact that retaining our top flight status is — to say the least — absolutely paramount.

There'll be ups and downs to come and I think our home form will be essential, but given the vein of sheer, raw emotion we tapped into against AZ Alkmaar, why can't we do that again and use it as the bedrock for a successful campaign?

Either way, it's going to be a hell of a ride!

articles.title: OTD (30/9/1944): When Sunderland Thrashed Newcastle 5-1 in a Wartime Derby
articles.summary: Sunderland travelled to St James’ Park in 1944 looking to repeat a home victory over Newcastle - but could anyone stop Cliff Whitelum on derby day?
articles.body:
A derby victory against Newcastle United is a prized event in any Sunderland player's career, and centre-forward Cliff Whitelum had good reason to remember this game.

At the start of the First World War in 1914, the Football League was not suspended, and many fans, footballers and officials had thought this an error. In hindsight, so did the Football League, and they were not about to make the same mistake again when World War II commenced in 1939. With the season just three games in, the Football League suspended all games.

Sunderland, like all other league clubs, suspended the contracts of all their players but retained their registrations.

Recognising a place for morale-boosting events (that could be fundraising opportunities as well), a regionalised competition played throughout England was organised within forty-eight days of the suspension of the league. Sunderland, along with Gateshead, Derby County, Ipswich Town and Aston Villa , at first declined to get involved. Initially, the belief at the club was that football was hardly the priority and all efforts needed to focus on defeating fascism.

It would be late March 1940 before Sunderland relented and played in some very local games.

In early June 1941, Sunderland's board agreed to get involved in the Wartime League North and the League War Cup. The plan was to give younger players encouragement and experience, as well as utilising the experience and skill of established older players.

All teams participating could call upon guest players who may have been stationed in their area if they had enlisted/been called up. Raich Carter, as a for instance, guested for Huddersfield and Derby County during the war years (as well as playing for Sunderland when available).

The availability or otherwise of experienced players often saw wildly swinging results, with teams losing then winning heavily in the return fixture sometimes just days later.

Johnny Cochrane offered nineteen-year-old Cliff Whitelum a professional contract after a trial match for Sunderland in 1938. It had been a rapid rise for a young man who had played no football until aged sixteen years old. He was asked to help out in an emergency for a local Co-operative Sports Club team (he was working in the grocery department). His progress was nothing if not astounding; he was playing for Bentley Colliery Welfare when invited to trial at Sunderland.

His professional career was in its infancy when war was declared. He had only played two games at centre-forward in 1938/39 in the first team, but he had scored a number of goals and shown up well in reserve team games.

Whitelum enlisted in the Royal Artillery and, following basic training, was posted to the Coastal Defence Anti-Aircraft Battery at Grangetown for the duration of the war. This battery, like many in the area, was heavily engaged in the fight against the Luftwaffe, who were frequent and unwelcome visitors.

What this posting did facilitate was fairly regular games for Sunderland in their wartime football campaigns for the developing forward. It could be said that he spent the war shooting at Nazi bombers and shooting for goals!

The situation also allowed him to play alongside some very good experienced Sunderland players, including Bobby Gurney, Raich Carter, Len Duns, Eddie Burbanks, Jimmy Gorman, Alex Hastings and Fred Hall, to name but a few.

Cliff Whitelum, at twenty-four years old, arrived into the 1944/45 season with ninety-nine wartime appearances behind him, having scored a quite remarkable ninety goals.

The start of this campaign had seen Sunderland win four and draw one of their first five games. Two of these victories had been won by five goals to one against Middlesbrough and Leeds , with Whitelum scoring a brace in each of these games.

Last time out, Sunderland had defeated Newcastle at Roker Park by two goals to nil, both goals coming from the rampant Whitelum.

And so it was to St James' Park for the return fixture in the War League North.

A crowd of 28,693 turned out to watch this contest, with Newcastle keen for revenge.

Both teams showed only one change from the previous game, so they would be reasonably familiar with each other heading into this contest.

Newcastle manager Stan Seymour had the experienced Bobby Cowell, Jimmy Gordon and Arsenal 's Eddie Carr guesting. They also had a bright young forward, who had been a Sunderland fan as a lad, called Jackie Milburn playing. Also playing in this game was a forward who had been an apprentice at Sunderland, Albert Stubbins. He had shown some promise when initially signed but had written into his contract that if his boyhood team came in for him, he could leave. That team was Newcastle, and in April 1937 he joined the Mags.

Despite his allegiances, Stubbins had actually guested for Sunderland in four previous wartime games, scoring two goals.

Manager Bill Murray had some experience playing with Johnny Spuhler, Jimmy Gorman, Alex Hastings and Alec Lockie. They also had right-half Harry Wallbanks guesting from Fulham and Fred Laidman, an inside-right from Bristol City.

A competitive, compelling first half saw Sunderland generally have the better of play and dominate possession for most of the half, but Newcastle had their moments.

With Spuhler and Walshaw on both wings causing a fair degree of consternation in the home defence, a neat passage of play saw Whitelum net the opener with a rocket of a shot on nine minutes.

At this point, Newcastle did well to stay in the game, with Sunderland's front five, egged on by half-backs Wallbanks and Hastings, threatening to run riot without quite managing to do so.

Newcastle had a spell of pressure coming in towards the end of the half, instigated by the hard-working inside-left Eddie Carr and inside-right Jackie Milburn in tandem. Milburn netted on forty minutes to send the home team into the dressing room a bit chirpier than they should have been given the flow of the game.

Any thoughts Newcastle had on avenging the previous week's defeat were quickly quashed upon resumption of the second half.

Whitelum scored within a minute of kick-off, with an almost identical goal to his first, as Sunderland proceeded to dominate the game. Ken Walshaw, stepping in off his wing, scored the Lads' third goal to cap a very good performance.

Newcastle did rally at this point, with Stubbins escaping his marker for the only time in the game to miss a relatively easy chance. Milburn and Carr got on the end of two shooting opportunities that might have yielded a score if luck had been on their side.

All resistance appeared to end when the excellent Johnny Spuhler netted on eighty-four minutes. Whitelum completed his hat-trick two minutes later to complete the rout and move Sunderland to the top of the War League North.

Alec Lockie had man-marked Albert Stubbins out of the game in a very good performance at centre-half. Half-backs Hastings and Wallbanks had outclassed their opposite numbers to provide a good flow of possession and passes to their front five, who had all enjoyed their afternoon, but none more so than the rampant Cliff Whitelum.

Albert Stubbins did go on to have better days, and after a transfer to Liverpool in 1946, he went on to score seventy-five goals for the Reds. He became the idol of a young Liverpool fan called Paul McCartney, who featured Stubbins on the album cover of Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band .

On the same day as this game, with the war in Europe going in the Allies' favour, Raich Carter scored a hat-trick for the British Services team, playing in Paris against France.

30,000 fans turned up to cheer both teams as Ted Drake got the other two goals.

Cliff Whitelum went on to score forty-two goals in thirty-six appearances in 1944/45. His wartime scoring record was 144 goals in 183 appearances.

The resumption of league football in 1946/47 brought new challenges and tighter defences to the free-scoring Whitelum. He finished joint-top scorer on seventeen goals alongside new signing Jackie Robinson, helping Sunderland to ninth position in the top tier.

After seven games and one goal in the 1947/48 season, Cliff Whitelum surprisingly left Sunderland for a record £9,000 fee to Sheffield United. The size of the fee offered and the emergence of Dickie Davis, a young forward who Murray signed just before the outbreak of the war, who had been guesting for Aston Villa and scored 74 goals in 60 games, probably triggered the transfer.

He made forty-three appearances, scoring a modest fourteen goals between 1947 and 1949 for the Blades, before moving to King's Lynn, where a former Blades team-mate was player/manager. Whitelum went on to score 237 goals in a 218-game career at King's Lynn, after which he signed for Stowmarket Town, where he scored 250 goals in his five seasons there before retiring.
