articles.title: Mitos de la Premier condenan al City por tramposo: "Si yo fuera jugador, tiraría esas medallas a la basura"
articles.standfirst: El siempre controvertido Roy Keane fue el exfutbolista que se mostró más duro y contundente contra el Manchester City
articles.summary: El siempre controvertido Roy Keane fue el exfutbolista que se mostró más duro y contundente contra el Manchester City
articles.body: Roy Keane, leyenda del Manchester United, afirma que tiraría sus medallas a la basura si fuera jugador del Manchester City, tras declararse al club 'cotizen' culpable de infringir las normas financieras de la Premier League durante nueve temporadas. "Sabían que esto haría daño a mucha gente, pero aun así lo hicieron. Si yo fuera jugador, tiraría esas medallas a la basura sin dudarlo. Por supuesto que lo haría; es hacer trampas... Ganaron en el campo porque se estaba haciendo trampa", aseguró Keane a ITV Sport tras la victoria de Inglaterra por 2-0 ante la República Checa en la Liga de Naciones. La Premier League afirma que el Manchester City concertó "contratos ficticios (que tergiversaban el acuerdo real entre las partes) con varios de sus socios comerciales, además de recurrir a acuerdos "ficticios" con otros, para inflar artificialmente los ingresos del club y reducir sus costes". También acusa al City de alterar falsamente su situación financiera por un valor de más de 1.050 millones de euros. El club había pactado acuerdos de patrocinio desorbitados con diversas empresas, pero dichos patrocinadores solo abonaban una parte de la cifra acordada. El resto era cubierto por Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), propietaria del club. Tal y como señala la Premier League, esto permitió al City "inflar artificialmente los ingresos del club" y, por consiguiente, gastar más conforme a la normativa de la competición. Roy Keane advirtió que teme que a la actual plantilla del City le resulte difícil mantener su nivel de rendimiento de élite bajo la sombra de unos "propietarios tramposos", que han sido declarados culpables de 114 de los 115 cargos presentados en su contra. "Creo que la situación será muy difícil para los jugadores, el entrenador (Enzo Maresca) y el club —y para lo que representan— cuando se tienen propietarios que no tienen reparos en hacer trampas. Es complicado mantener un nivel de excelencia", apuntó el controvertido exfutbolista de 55 años. Ian Wrigth, leyenda del Arsenal, apuntó que "les decían que no ocurría nada malo. Pero, como jugador, te das cuenta de que algo no encaja". "Aquí se requiere una sanción sin precedentes. Es un día crucial para la Premier League. Es un asunto muy turbio", apuntó Wright pidiendo una dura sanción para el Manchester City. Wayne Rooney, leyenda del Manchester United que perdió una Premier contra el City en la temporada 2011-2012, declaró en el podcast 'Stick to United' que no quiere que se le otorgue el título con carácter retroactivo en el caso de que el Manchester City finalmente sea sancionado. "Para ser sincero, no me sentiría cómodo aceptando otra medalla de la Premier League, porque no creo que la merezcamos. No hicimos lo suficiente esa temporada para ganar la Premier", compartió. Rooney se sinceró sobre sus sentimientos por las trampas del City: "Pienso en sus jugadores: ellos están ahí haciendo todo lo posible por ganar el título de la Premier League y, en su mente, ya lo han conseguido. Y si esos jugadores no tienen conocimiento de lo que ocurre en los despachos, entonces —si me pasara a mí, si de repente el Manchester United hubiera hecho lo mismo y me quitaran mis medallas de la Premier League— estaría absolutamente destrozado". "Podrían quitárselas, pero yo no lo querría, porque no siento que como equipo lo mereciéramos aquel año, ya que obviamente no terminamos primeros", apuntó.

articles.title: John Stones convicted after missing police speeding letter while playing at World Cup
articles.summary: Stones was at the wheel of a Range Rover when it was clocked by a speed camera going at 43mph on a 30mph road
articles.body:
Footballer John Stones has been convicted of speeding and hit with a court bill after he missed a police letter while at the World Cup.

The 32-year-old defender, who joined Inter Milan in the summer, was caught driving his £150,000 Range Rover at 43mph along a country lane near his Cheshire mansion in May.

Stones admitted being the driver when first contacted by Cheshire Police , but did not respond to a second letter offering him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court.

He was then prosecuted and convicted in the Single Justice Procedure, with a magistrate last week issuing him four penalty points and ordering him to pay a £666 fine, £120 in costs, and a £266 victim surcharge.

Explaining the mishap, Stones wrote to Warrington Magistrates Court to say: "Nothing to say about the speeding.

"The reason I am only responding to the offence now is because I represent our country for football and so I have not been home and seen any post.

"I sent off my letter on the 28th May to give my details, I went off to join England .

"I went on holiday and then moved to Milan, so this has been found by chance, as no one has been home for almost four months.

"This is the reason I also would not be able to be present as I no longer am residing in the country."

Court records show Stones was at the wheel of a Range Rover when it was clocked by a speed camera going at 43mph on a 30mph stretch of road.

The incident happened at 10.40am on May 8, just as Manchester City was in the final stages of last season's title race and preparing for the FA Cup final.

Stones started the first match of the World Cup finals in the USA after being selected in the 26-man squad; he featured again in the quarter-final clash with Mexico and played in England 's semi-final defeat to Argentina .

articles.body: Musab Al-Shaqsi marcó en el minuto 84 para poner a Omán 3-1 por delante de Kuwait; esta victoria permitía a Omán igualar a Irak con 4 puntos en la Copa del Golfo, además de empatar la diferencia de goles a favor y en contra. Antes de la celebración Omán tenía ventaja sobre Irak gracias al criterio de desempate disciplinario de 'Fair Play' (7 tarjetas amarillas frente a las 8 de Irak), pero al quitarse la camiseta en la celebración del gol Musab Al-Shaqsi fue sancionado con amarilla. La sanción a Musab Al-Shaqsi anuló de forma automática la única ventaja que poseía el conjunto omaní sobre el iraquí. Con esa tarjeta Irán y Omán empataban 8-8 a amarillas, por lo que el equipo de Musab Al-Shaqsi perdió su ventaja y condenó a Omán a un sorteo. Afortunadamente para Musab Al-Shaqsi su selección ganó el sorteo que se celebró en un hotel y se clasificó para las semifinales de la Copa del Golfo.

articles.title: Marc Roca: "Me siento en mi mejor momento personal y futbolístico"
articles.standfirst: El catalán dejó atrás sus problemas de tobillo y ya es un fijo para Pellegrini en la medular
articles.summary: El catalán dejó atrás sus problemas de tobillo y ya es un fijo para Pellegrini en la medular
articles.body: Marc Roca se ha convertido en una de las buenas noticias del arranque de temporada del Betis. Olvidada ya la lesión de tobillo que le lastró durante algún tiempo y asumiendo un rol más posicional en la medular verdiblanca, el centrocampista catalán es un fijo para Pellegrini y afronta con ambición y optimismo un curso marcado por el regreso a la Champions. Así lo explica en una entrevista en Betis TV. Un largo parón de selecciones: "La verdad que es raro, ¿no? Después de comenzar la competición con tantos partidos tan exigentes en Liga y en Champions, ahora estas tres semanas sin fútbol se nos hacen un poco raras a nosotros. Imagino que a vosotros también, ¿no? Pero bueno, hay que adaptarse a lo que hay. Es verdad que se hace largo porque al final estamos con ganas de competir. Estábamos disfrutando mucho, pero ha tocado de esta manera esta vez; toca adaptarse y continuar". El equipo prefería seguir compitiendo: "Sí, obviamente el equipo ha empezado muy bien, hemos empezado todos súper bien, así que nos hubiera gustado que eso continuara. Estábamos con muy buenas sensaciones, seguimos estándolo, así que ahora seguimos entrenando y preparando lo que viene, que tampoco parará". Buenas sensaciones: "Sí, la verdad que muy feliz, muy contento. Me siento jugando a un muy buen nivel. Creo que el equipo está jugando muy bien, afrontando todos los partidos con mucha intensidad y con un buen fútbol. Estamos disfrutando dentro del campo y creo que la afición también lo está notando cuando jugamos en casa. Estamos notando mucho su apoyo, que al final será muy importante a lo largo de la temporada. Así que contentos y disfrutando de este momento". Cumplió 100 partidos con el Betis: "Sí, obviamente cumplir 100 partidos con el Real Betis creo que es espectacular. Ya son unas cuantas temporadas aquí vistiendo la camiseta y me siento desde el primer día como en casa. Me siento muy especial y muy querido por la gente, así que contento y feliz". Un escalón más en su cuarta temporada: "Sí, la verdad que creo que el club está creciendo muchísimo. Yo lo he vivido durante estos cuatro años que no para de crecer. Creo que esto es muy importante para nosotros y para la entidad. Ojalá siga así porque creo que tenemos una plantilla muy buena, margen de crecimiento, mucha ambición y queremos ir a por más". Una base sólida hasta llegar a Champions: "Sí, creo que al final las cosas grandes se forjan paso a paso, con un buen equilibrio y con una buena estructura. Creo que el míster ha conseguido hacer una buena base y unos buenos cimientos, y a partir de ahí puedes ir construyendo. Se está notando que el equipo está en un muy buen momento. Estamos a un gran nivel y disfrutando con ganas y con la sensación de que estamos muy bien, pero que aún podemos hacerlo mejor, así que creo que eso es muy positivo". La motivación de la Champions: "Con mucha ilusión. Creo que es la mejor competición a nivel de clubes. Cuando llegué aquí, para mí era un sueño volver a jugar la Champions y disfrutarla. Creo que este año es para jugarla, disfrutarla y soñar en grande, porque al final en esta vida tienes que soñar en grande y después ya veremos hasta dónde llegamos. Pero creo que el equipo está con una buena mentalidad. La afición ya vemos que estará en todos los campos llenos, así que siempre tenemos la suerte de tenerlos a nuestro lado. Es muy ilusionante, muy motivante y estamos con ganas de hacer algo grande". Doble visita a Alemania: "Sí, son estadios de mucha historia, estadios grandes y de muchas noches europeas. Tanto el del Dortmund como el del Bayern son dos equipos espectaculares, muy grandes, y son partidos para ir a competir. Creo que tenemos equipo para ir de tú a tú. Antes tenemos partidos importantes en casa y creo que es donde nos tenemos que hacer fuertes en esta competición. Sabemos que cada vez que vas fuera de casa es muy complicado. Hablando de Champions, contra el Oporto y contra el Feyenoord tenemos que ir a sumar muchos puntos porque ahí estará la base". Calendario apretado y cuatro partidos seguidos en casa: "Sí, total. Al final estamos acostumbrados a jugar cada tres o cuatro días, llevamos muchos años haciéndolo. La plantilla es larga y amplia para hacer rotaciones, porque es importante que los jugadores estemos frescos y preparados para cuando nos toque. No es ninguna excusa, es una oportunidad para hacer grandes cosas. Cuatro partidos en casa con nuestra afición es donde nos tenemos que hacer fuertes y seguir para arriba". Muchas alternativa sen el centro del campo: "Sí, tal cual. Tenemos una competencia muy sana. Lo más importante es el equipo y que cada jugador al que le toque jugar dé el máximo nivel y le demuestre al míster que está para jugar. A partir de ahí el míster decide. Hay mucho nivel y mucha competencia, pero nos entendemos muy bien entre todos. Lo hemos estado demostrando en todos los partidos y eso es muy sano para el equipo y para el crecimiento". Con compañeros a los que conoce desde la sub 21: "Sí, vivimos muchos momentos juntos, muy buenos y de mucho disfrute, donde fuimos campeones de Europa sub-21. Jugar al lado de Pablo (Fornals), de Dani (Ceballos) en este caso, y en el pasado con Fabián, es un disfrute porque son jugadores de mucho nivel que quieren siempre la pelota, y eso es lo que a mí me gusta como mediocentro. Estoy muy contento y muy feliz de que estén aquí". Ceballos, poniéndose a punto: "Sí, está entrenando fuerte y cogiendo un buen ritmo para poder competir al 100%, y la verdad que lo esperamos con los brazos abiertos. Sabemos de la calidad de Dani, del jugador que es y que nos va a ayudar muchísimo, así que estamos con muchísimas ganas". Amistoso solidario frente al Ceuta: "Sí, obviamente. Es un parón muy largo y atípico, no estamos acostumbrados a tener un parón tan largo tras jugar varias jornadas de Liga. Pero nos vendrá bien el jueves competir para exigir a nuestro cuerpo a estar a buen ritmo y nivel, para afrontar el partido de Osasuna con las mejores garantías. Es un partido en casa bonito para disfrutarlo". Unos días de descanso con su familia: "Hay que aprovechar para estar un poquito en la montaña y por casa con la familia, así que contento y con las pilas cargadas. Al final también es un parón para seguir trabajando porque hay que prepararse bien; hay muchos partidos y el cuerpo hay que prepararlo para las exigencias que vengan, así que hay que aprovecharlo". No deja de entrenar ni en vacaciones: "Al final es un estilo de vida. A mí me gusta trabajar y entrenar; llevo muchos años entrenando muy fuerte por las tardes. Creo que es importante a nivel físico preparar tu cuerpo al 100% para poder competir. Yo me lo tomo de esta manera, otros compañeros se lo tomarán de otra, pero estoy contento de hacerlo así. Es mi forma de vida y mi mentalidad". El más disciplinado de la plantilla: "Creo que el fútbol a día de hoy, aparte de ser un deporte muy táctico y muy técnico, es muy físico. Jugando cada tres o cuatro días se incrementa este nivel y tienes que estar preparado. Yo me preparo para estar siempre disponible para el míster e intentar siempre mejorar: ser más rápido, más fuerte, saltar más... pequeños detalles que te ayudan a competir mejor". Su lesión, olvidada: "Sí, eso ya ha quedado atrás. Gracias a Dios me siento muy bien del tobillo y físicamente. A lo largo de mi vida he tenido varias lesiones que solo me han hecho más fuerte y me han ayudado a seguir trabajando, focalizarme y crecer. No me lo he tomado nunca como algo negativo, sino como una oportunidad para seguir creciendo física y mentalmente. Ahora, a mis 29 años, me siento muy bien mental y físicamente, preparado y disfrutando mucho". En plena madurez futbolística: "Sobre todo me siento muy bien y muy cómodo, contento conmigo mismo y con mi vida. Es una muy buena edad porque ya tienes experiencia. Físicamente tenemos suplementación, alimentación y muchos recursos para recuperar más rápido. Antes a los 32 o 33 años estabas casi para la retirada, pero ahora el fútbol se está alargando mucho y es una edad ideal. Yo me siento en mucho equilibrio, contento y feliz". El mejor momento de su carrera: "Sí, sobre todo hablando del tiempo que he estado aquí en el Betis. Me siento en mi mejor momento personal y futbolístico. Sufrí mucho por el tobillo izquierdo en el pasado, lo que me generaba mucho estrés y me obligaba a entrenar y competir con dolor y antiinflamatorios, y eso era un no vivir a nivel mental. Ahora que físicamente estoy limpio, mentalmente estoy mucho más fuerte, preparado y capacitado para afrontar todo lo que viene por delante". Una temporada para soñar: "Sí, por supuesto. Hay que soñar en grande. Hay una plantilla muy buena y una afición maravillosa. El equipo está en crecimiento constante, queremos más y todo el mundo quiere subirse al barco. Sabemos que es una carrera de fondo y que la temporada es muy larga, pero hay que ir partido a partido y darlo todo en los entrenamientos. Estamos preparados para hacer una gran temporada e ilusionante para todos. Si vienen momentos difíciles, pedimos unión porque juntos los sacaremos rápido y seguro que será un año increíble para todos".

articles.title: "El problema de Lamine Yamal es que no juega en el Madrid"
articles.standfirst: Ferran Martínez saca la cara por el jugador del Barcelona y señala por qué hay quién pone en duda al joven futbolista
articles.summary: Ferran Martínez saca la cara por el jugador del Barcelona y señala por qué hay quién pone en duda al joven futbolista
articles.body: David Bernabéu, Pedro Riesco, Látigo Serrano, Jorge Segura, Jorge Liaño y Ferran Martínez han sido los tertulianos de este miércoles en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por la victoria de la selección española ante Croacia otra vez con Lamine en el foco. David Bernabéu. "La selección española no ha tenido jamás un futbolista como Lamine Yamal. ¿Cuántos futbolistas ha hecho lo que ha hecho Lamine de los 15 a los 19 años? Cojo y sin estar a su nivel es mejor que el resto. Estamos ante un acontecimiento histórico, es un futbolista que nunca ha existido en el fútbol español: un crack mundial en el campo, a nivel mediático, que vas a Estados Unidos y estaba en tres de cada cuatro rascacielos y que marca las diferencias en el campo. El problema es que juega en el Barça". Pedro Riesco. "Claro que hay gente que reniega de Lamine Yamal. Os habéis encargado de compararle durante mucho tiempo cn el gran Vinicius y tiene 19 años. El problema de Lamine Yamal es que viste de blaugrana". Látigo Serrano. "Este año Lamine va a volver a doblar sus cifras. Es evidente que va a ganar más de cinco Balones de Oro. Y si no hay nada que le aparte del fútbol, que se quiera dedicar a la canción como Jesé, una novia que le diga que tiene que estar con ella y dejar esto del fútbol, una lesión grave... si no pasa nada extraño, va a ganar cinco Balones de Oro y seis Champions". Jorge Segura. "A muchos periodistas y a muchos medios de comunicación les molesta el hecho de que Lamine sea jugador del Barcelona. El Mundial de Lamine fue discreto para el nivel que tiene". Jorge Liaño. "Lamine Yamal lo ha ganado todo. Y su gran rival, Mbappé, no ha ganado nada porque desde 2018 no gana nada, un título menor que es la liga francesa y alguna copita francesa. ¿Con quién queréis que lo comparemos? ¿Con Kane? Pues el otro día ganó a Kane". Ferran Martínez. "El problema de Lamines es que viste de azulgrana, que juega en el Barça y que no juega en el Madrid. Os duele que el mejor jugador del mundo es del Barça y formado en La Masía, eso os crea un cortocircuito en la cabeza porque juega en la selección española. Antes no había problema porque jugaba con Argentina, pero ahora juega con España".

articles.title: Man City Premier League charges: Jamie Carragher says club's titles should be stripped and owners removed
articles.summary: Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023
articles.body:
City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

During the period between the 2009/10 season and 2017/18 season, City won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield.

"I do think Manchester City's titles they've won in this time, or trophies, should be taken off their list," Sky Sports pundit Carragher said.

However, Carragher is less convinced whether those honours should then be passed onto teams and players who finished second to City in those competitions. Ultimately, he says, the most important part of winning in football - the feeling at the time - has been taken from those players, clubs and their fans by City's actions.

"Whether other clubs should get them is slightly different," said Carragher. "But what Manchester City have done is, they've not just hurt their own players in terms of no one looks at their trophies and medals now in the same way...

"I've been very lucky to win a few medals. I never look at the medal years later. But my mind goes back to a moment, I get a feeling in my stomach. I remember the referee blowing a final whistle of a big game.

"Those players will never get that feeling and it was robbed by Manchester City. That's what they haven't got. I don't think any player will care if you go and give them a medal, and he puts it in the house, in his trophy room, he'll never look at it.

"It's not about medals, it's about feelings, and that's what Manchester City have robbed."

Carragher says while he expects Man City as a club to be punished, the owners must pay for their involvement by losing their leadership roles.

"The club are going to get punished," he said. "You've got supporters, players, the club and owners. For me this is all about the owners, the people who are at the top of the club.

"Man City are a wonderful club and have been for a hundred years and will be for hundreds of years going forward. But in terms of what we're finding out now, I don't know how the owners can continue in English football.

"We talk about a fit and proper test for owners. What they've done for 10 years - and left this stain that will be there for the next 10 years - it starts because they don't like the word no. When you see the statements - the one from [CEO Ferran] Soriano last night - it's beggars belief what you're hearing.

"They have so much power and finance behind them, nobody ever tells them no. Until they move away from the club, I don't know how this stain is removed from the club.

"City will move on - they will have great teams in the future. But I don't see how the ownership can continue after what's happened here and their reaction to it. How can they be surprised? They've got irrefutable evidence - well where is it? Put it out there."

Carra: If I was a City player 'I'd be furious'

Carragher also discussed what the news means for the legacy of City's greatest players of the period and the current squad, saying he is sympathetic to their situation, even if some former players are continuing to defend City's actions right now.

"I'd be furious and I actually feel for the Man City players," said Carragher. "As a team, what they've done is wrong. The Premier League have called it a sham five times in their statement.

"But in terms of individual players, some of them are coming out to bat for the club, that's normal right now. It must be very difficult for them to see anything that's going on and to almost feel like a lot of their career is going to have an asterisk with it, or people are just going to call it a sham.

"I think of Kevin De Bruyne, who's one of the greatest players I've ever seen. He could have played for any team in the world and he still would have been one of the best players. He was fantastic.

"But he chose his club to be Manchester City. Now, one of those reasons he may have chosen, maybe was his wages, that maybe were inflated because of the situation around Man City and what they've been charged with.

"But if he sits there at the end of his career now and the whole world looks at his Manchester City career of 10 years of service and look at it as a sham, and I keep using that word, that's the word the Premier League used, I'd be furious. Absolutely furious that around the world people are looking at my career like that because of what's going on upstairs.

"Those people have continually told those players - because I have spoken to certain players about it - that everything was fine. They were not going to get done for anything.

"We keep talking about Liverpool or Manchester United, all these players who maybe could get Premier League titles now. And that's absolutely spot on

"But I've actually been thinking about the Manchester City players and how they feel. What Manchester City's hierarchy are coming out with in the last couple of days as well, they're just gaslighting the players, their ex-players, their supporters, because those people want to believe them so much. They've got such strong relationships with them, they want to believe it right now.

"I think the longer this goes on, the more you'll see less support from maybe ex-City players and more frustration about maybe how their careers are going to be viewed by the outside world."

articles.title: Rangers transfers: Inside the summer window that lay foundations for consecutive Celtic wins - but will it deliver long-term success?
articles.summary: The Ibrox club focussed on physicality and speed over the summer, whilst reducing the squad's average age; Rangers also targeted signings they believe can grow in value; Derek McInnes' side beat Celtic twice before the international break to make it six consecutive wins after a tough start
articles.body:
His first four games were winless, followed by that humiliating European exit to Jablonec .

However, when Rangers return from the international break, they will have their sights set on going top of the Scottish Premiership for the first time this season.

That's down to a new-look squad and six consecutive wins, including back-to-back Old Firm victories . There is a feel-good factor in the stands at Ibrox once again.

Here, we look at how a key summer transfer window helped pave the way for a remarkable turnaround - one McInnes knows he must keep on track against Kilmarnock on October 10.

Before we get into the fine detail, it's important to take a look at the bigger picture.

This was the second consecutive summer that Rangers signed 14 players. However, the two windows couldn't be more different.

For full context, you need to go back 12 months. It was a new era (yes, another one) at Ibrox. Russell Martin had been appointed head coach, and the club were being led by CEO Patrick Stewart and sporting director Kevin Thelwell. However, that fresh start proved to be a false dawn.

As Rangers went off track, Martin was sacked after 123 days , before Stewart and Thelwell followed soon after . Meanwhile, of the 14 signings sanctioned by the likes of the aforementioned, only four remain. Chairman Andrew Cavenagh admitted mistakes had been made, and after issuing the P45's, he took a more hands-on role at the club.

Some might think it was Robbie Thelwell, who has the title "head of recruitment", who was in charge of the signings. In truth, his title does not reflect his responsibility, and he works in the scouting team.

Instead, fast-forward 12 months and working alongside Cavenagh were the likes of CEO Jim Gillespie, who joined in March , now outgoing technical director Dan Purdy , Paraag Marathe and Gretar Steinsson of the 49ers, plus Stig Inge Bjornebye, who was appointed performance director in June following a spell as consultant.

Rangers were not only looking at players' attributes, but also how they'd fit in the dressing room, their injury history, trading value and so on. Things which in the past were not always prioritised but are now all part of the equation.

The likes of Purdy would identify the options, Cavenagh and Gillespie were among those signing off on the deals, all done with the backing of the 49ers and ultimately the manager.

While there will always be successes and failures, this time Rangers had a united approach.

Rangers' initial target was to sign fewer players than they did the previous summer, but opportunities and injuries saw that number rise from around 10 to 14.

The club's leadership group set the parameters, the model of how Rangers should play both domestically and in Europe was in place, and it was over to the new powers that be to sign the players - just like they did in January when Tuur Rommens, Tochi Chukwuani and Ryan Naderi were permanent additions.

Rangers' goal this season - under McInnes, who knows the Scottish game inside out - was to taste domestic success once again.

So what was the plan to end Celtic's Premiership stranglehold? Well, rather than trying to copy their Old Firm rivals' possession-based style of play, Rangers were focussing on physicality and speed. The view was that to beat Celtic, they couldn't be like Celtic - they had to work differently.

Furthermore, following the departures of captain James Tavernier, vice-captain Jack Butland and co, they needed leaders in the squad, plus wanted to reduce the overall age of the group - something they had achieved over the previous windows.

Finally, while chairman Cavenagh was willing to splash the cash for the right players, many signings would still need to have the potential to grow in value and help the club flourish.

It was a complex checklist and not everything has been fixed at Ibrox over a few months. This was always going to take multiple windows. However, there are positive signs.

The average age of the team that beat Celtic in their two games before the international break was less than 24 - compared to their rivals, who were closer to 27.

The starting XI in those games comprised of a new-look spine and six summer signings: goalkeeper Ivor Pandur, defender Olwethu Makhanya, captain Dan Neil in midfield along with James Penrice, Minsu Kim out wide and Kevin Kelsy leading the line.

At Ibrox in their League Cup quarter-final triumph, Rangers played like a team with an identity and style. They were strong, physical, fast and dominated the battle for second balls. That was reaffirmed at Parkhead in the Premiership a week later, while their rivals changed shape in a search for answers that didn't arrive.

Both in January and this summer, Rangers have been adding to their squad with a clear plan in place. They now have a group boasting speed, physicality, desire and the types of players who could attract interest from bigger leagues across Europe.

That recognition is coming on the international front too, with 13 of the squad selected by their country for this three-week window. Of those away with their countries, 12 of the 13 are 26 or under too - a clear sign of the change in direction at Ibrox.

There has been significant work to alter Rangers' recruitment process since last summer, and while the early signs are positive, nothing is won in September.

Rangers still need to catch Celtic in the Premiership and face a tough test in Aberdeen, if they're to book a spot in the League Cup final, where Hearts or Hibs would await.

However, for the first time in years, after a busy transfer window and consecutive Old Firm victories - they head into Autumn with a platform that will allow them to deliver.

articles.title: Tebas responde a RMTV mostrando que el Real Madrid pagó a la misma empresa que el Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El presidente de LaLiga ha publicado unas facturas en las que el club blanco transfirió dinero a Audiovisual New Aged, sociedad vinculada al presidente de LaLiga
articles.summary: El presidente de LaLiga ha publicado unas facturas en las que el club blanco transfirió dinero a Audiovisual New Aged, sociedad vinculada al presidente de LaLiga
articles.body: Javier Tebas volvió a cargar contra el Real Madrid a través de las redes sociales. El presidente de LaLiga respondió en X a una publicación de un usuario que compartió un vídeo de Real Madrid TV relacionado con un documento del Barcelona sobre un préstamo de 4,5 millones de euros a Audiovisual New Aged, una sociedad vinculada al propio Tebas. En su respuesta, el dirigente de LaLiga puso el foco en unas operaciones realizadas anteriormente por el club blanco con esa misma empresa. Tebas aseguró que dispone de documentación que acredita dichas transferencias y afirmó: "Adjunto dos ejemplos de transferencias del Real Madrid a Audiovisual New Aged. Entre 2011 y 2013, las transferencias del club a esta sociedad sumaron 7.513.333,55 euros. Sí, a la misma sociedad a la que aportaba el FC Barcelona. ¡Qué sorpresa!". Tebas también reclamó explicaciones a dos personas relacionadas con el Real Madrid por el motivo de aquellas operaciones. "Pregunten a JAS y a Chitín del Valle por qué se hicieron esas transferencias y cuál era su finalidad. Y que Chitín explique también el correo del 9 de mayo de 2018 y quien le dio las instrucciones para ese correo", escribió. El presidente de LaLiga fue un paso más allá y pidió que la documentación sea trasladada al Real Madrid para que el club vuelva a pronunciarse públicamente sobre el asunto. "Hazles llegar los documentos, @AdriiRM33, y que hagan otro vídeo. Esta vez explicando lo que ahora ocultan. Continuará… basta de mentir, manipular...", concluyó Tebas.

articles.title: Martin Drury exclusive: Meet the former Man Utd and Valencia coach plotting Huddersfield's way out of League One
articles.summary: Martin Drury on beating Real Madrid at the Bernabeu, why he left Brentford, going back to his roots in Huddersfield and wanting his team to possess northern spirit; watch Burton vs Huddersfield live on Sky Sports+ on Saturday October 3; kick-off 3pm
articles.body:
Martin Drury is a straight-talking man, open about the fact it was never in his plans to become a head coach.

Granted, he was in charge of Bradford Park Avenue in the National League North for much of 2015/16, but that came quite shortly after his retirement and he soon disappeared into the background.

Over the next decade, he built a coaching career that took in spells at Boston United, Bradford City, Manchester United, West Brom and Valencia.

Now at Huddersfield - the team of the town in which he was born - he is in charge in his own right. An interim spell from March led to a two-year deal in May.

Here, he tells Sky Sports about his journey from LaLiga to the Premier League to plotting the Terriers' way out of League One.

Drury met Carlos Corberan while he was at Bradford and the Spaniard was at Leeds. The two began to work together in August 2024 when Drury was appointed individual coach at West Brom.

"When I first met Carlos, I felt we connected from a work ethic perspective and we were very much aligned in how we saw life and earning everything you get in life through work," he says.

"On the football side, we were very much aligned on what we believed in and what we truly believed we could do with players. I think we have some similar characteristics, despite being from different cultures."

Corberan left for Valencia on Christmas Eve 2024 and Drury followed within a matter of days after being appointed as his assistant. A Championship play-off push was sacrificed for the challenge of keeping Los Murcielagos in LaLiga.

They almost had the perfect start, leading Real Madrid at the Mestalla until the 85th minute on January 3 2025, when Luka Modric levelled and Jude Bellingham scored the 96th-minute winner.

"I remember prepping for that game and thinking this was the type of environment I wanted to be in, to go up against players like Kylian Mbappe, Bellingham, Modric.

"To play them again at the back end of the season and win 2-1 - in the last minute, in the Bernabeu - was naturally the highlight and the connection between us and the fans there was something so, so special.

"We suffered in both of the games against Barcelona, but to see the quality of player at that level in the flesh and to prep for those games against some of the best managers in the world, the best players in the world, on a weekly basis, was something I loved."

"When we arrived, the club were rock bottom of the league and to finish so close to Europe by the end of the season, having picked up some points against giants was pretty special.

'Sometimes you have to assess whether you're the one for a club'

Drury was tempted back to the UK in July 2025, when he was appointed as one of Keith Andrews' assistant first-team coaches at Brentford.

But by early September, after just three Premier League games, he departed. "Martin has played an important role in setting us up for the season ahead," said director of football Phil Giles.

"It's an amazing club with brilliant people and I don't think you can do anything but respect what they do," says Drury.

"They're outstanding from top to bottom. Keith has done an unbelievable job and I really enjoyed it there.

"Sometimes in football, you just have to assess whether it's the one for you and whether you're the right one for the club.

"The conversations I had there were really open and honest, but I look at them from afar and I'm so happy with how they went last season.

"I genuinely think they'll be even stronger this season because Keith is a top manager, they've got a really good group of players and the club is run impeccably well from top to bottom."

The premature departure from west London brought an unplanned pause in Drury's career.

"I moved back up north to be close to my family and it was the first time in 12 years I'd spent a little bit of time outside of football… which I absolutely despised!" he says, only half-joking.

"I'd not really had a break for 10 to 12 years, so I jumped out of that hamster wheel and, when I look back, it was quite productive in terms of connecting with people I'd not seen for a while, going and seeing different things, challenging myself and my thinking.

"I had a couple of opportunities to go into different clubs, but I said no because I felt I needed a little bit longer, then I was really fortunate to get a call from Liam Manning, who asked me to come into Huddersfield with him.

"I'd known Liam a little while before that and Huddersfield's close to my heart, so I was looking forward to coming in and looking to build something special."

In January 2026, Drury was appointed assistant manager to Manning and, in late March, along with Jon Stead, he stepped up to take charge when Manning was given compassionate leave.

A statement from on the club's official website said: "Liam made the club aware of ongoing personal matters relating to the tragic passing of his newborn son Theo in October 2024".

Huddersfield won two and drew four of the seven games Drury led, missing out on the League One play-offs by eight points.

'When I believe in something, I can feel very strongly about it'

Drury's permanent appointment came on May 27. The club said he had established himself as the "outstanding" candidate.

In spite of his lack of prior desire to be in charge in his own right, he was all in on the project.

"I love coaching, I love being on the grass, I love working with players - but I'm pretty driven and when I really believe in something, I can feel very strongly about it.

"In the back of my mind I thought, at some point, if I feel so strongly about a certain way of working, a culture and an environment that I want to create, maybe I was going to have to do this from the front. That wasn't something I was concentrating on, but you can never be too surprised in football.

"When the opportunity became apparent, the decision was really clear for me.

"When there was a little bit of turbulence towards the end of the season, I never felt it was a real challenging environment to work in or difficult people to work with. I felt there were a lot of people who wanted the best for the club.

"The fact we've now had one window and we've been able to address some areas of the group we wanted to try and strengthen, I think the players who were here last season have probably appreciated the work that's gone on because it's going to help them.

"There's some connection building in the group; that's going to take some more time, as it always does when you bring in new players. But it's a real humble group of men where, every day, the environment is driven by development, with a real winning edge and a competitive focus on it."

Drury knows what he wants - he wants his team to epitomise the spirit of the north.

"When I'm standing on the side of the pitch, I want to see a team that represents Huddersfield. I want to see players running and giving absolutely everything," he adds.

"Being a northern lad myself, I know what these northern fans want.

"If we do that, I have genuine belief that, because of the players and staff we have, success will be achieved."

articles.body:
After a wild Saturday in the Football Bowl Subdivision, Week 5 provides an opportunity to take a collective breath.

Don't mistake that for a lack of marquee games, though.

Many college football teams—six of them in the AP Top 25—have an open date. It's a chance for those rosters to rest and prepare for a long, challenging run through conference play.

Nevertheless, three ranked matchups highlight the weekend, with seven Top 10 teams hitting the road. Chaos is always lurking.

No. 7 Alabama (4-0) at No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0), Noon ET

Knocking off Missouri was good and important. Shifting from "fun story" to "genuine threat" in the SEC, however, requires Mississippi State taking down Alabama. Kamario Taylor, a dynamic playmaker, deserves the hype. But there is still reason to be concerned about MSU's defense, which surrendered 400-plus yards to both South Carolina and Mizzou.

Prediction : Alabama 34, Mississippi State 24

No. 5 Ohio State (3-1) at No. 14 Iowa (4-0), 3:30 p.m.

Despite Iowa dominating the all-time series, Ohio State certainly hasn't forgotten a shocking 55-24 loss at Kinnick Stadium in 2017. There shouldn't be a repeat. Ohio State should be able to silence Iowa's offense. However, any trip to Iowa City deserves a mountain of respect.

No. 8 Florida (4-0) at No. 25 Missouri (3-1), 3:30 p.m.

Missouri has yielded 100.3 rushing yards per game at a paltry 2.7 per carry. If that run defense shows up Saturday afternoon, Mizzou has a real chance to spring an upset. Otherwise, Florida will be able to control the clock and open a season with a 5-0 record for the first time since 2019.

No. 4 Miami (4-0) at Clemson (3-1), 7:30 p.m.

Yet another Top 10 team on the road, Miami is poised to meet Clemson in a critical ACC game. Although the mood around Clemson is subpar, the Tigers are 2-0 in conference play and could shatter expectations with an upset. That's just not something I'm willing to project, given Clemson's struggles to find explosive plays and the upside of the Darian Mensah-led Miami offense.

Pitt (4-0) at Virginia Tech (4-0), Friday, 7 p.m. ET

Neither team is ranked, yet both are unbeaten. The winner of this matchup will be a serious contender in the ACC, especially since Miami eventually has to take on Pitt and Virginia Tech, too. I'll lean toward a raucous home-field advantage here, but Pitt is a balanced, dangerous visitor.

articles.title: El Rayo anuncia la vuelta a su estadio para disputar el Trofeo de Vallecas
articles.standfirst: El club franjirrojo jugará contra el Cagliari el próximo sábado 3 de octubre en su sede por primera vez en la temporada
articles.summary: El club franjirrojo jugará contra el Cagliari el próximo sábado 3 de octubre en su sede por primera vez en la temporada
articles.body: La vuelta al estadio de Vallecas ya tiene fecha. El sábado 3 de octubre a las 14:00 horas (horario peninsular), el Rayo Vallecano se medirá al Cagliari en un encuentro amistoso para disputar el trofeo de Vallecas. Este histórico trofeo se disputará por primera vez después de siete años y será la primera vez que el equipo de Beñat San José juegue en su estadio esta temporada. La última vez que se jugó el Trofeo de Vallecas fue en 2019 cuando se enfrentaron el Alcorcón. Precisamente, el club del sur de Madrid fue el que se llevó la victoria por 3-2. El Rayo lo defenderá, esta vez, ante el equipo italiano que va cuarto en Serie A. El club lo ha anunciado con una publicación en la que anuncian que los abonados tendrán pase libre y las entradas variarán entre los 10 y los 35 euros. Las taquillas estarán abiertas el miércoles 30 de septiembre de 15 a 20 horas, el jueves 1 de octubre y el viernes 2 de octubre, de 11 a 20 horas y el día del partido desde las 11 hasta el comienzo del encuentro. Este torneo se disputó por primera vez en el año 1970 con el enfrentamiento entre el Rayo Vallecano y el Atlético de Madrid. En el año 1985 el trofeo pasó a denominarse Trofeo Alcampo por la publicidad de la marca de supermercados, y en 2002, durante la época de los Ruiz-Mateos, pasó a llamarse Trofeo Teresa Rivero. En 2011, después de la llegada de Raúl Martín Presa, se volvió a cambiar la denominación del trofeo para llamarse Trofeo de Vallecas. El fútbol vuelve al estadio de Vallecas para jugarse uno de los trofeos más queridos por la afición.

articles.title: El Castellón, un equipo de ataque con defensa de acero
articles.standfirst: El conjunto albinegro solo ha encajado dos goles en siete jornadas
articles.summary: El conjunto albinegro solo ha encajado dos goles en siete jornadas
articles.body: El Castellón ha encontrado el equilibrio perfecto en este inicio de temporada con una propuesta ofensiva eficaz que ha estado acompañada por una solidez notable en la retaguardia, lo que le ha llevado a liderar la tabla de Segunda. El conjunto albinegro es el segundo máximo realizador del campeonato, con 14 goles, y el segundo que más ha disparado a puerta, con 38 tiros. Pero también es el que mejores números defensivos tiene. Porque los de Pablo Hernández sólo han encajado dos tantos en siete jornadas, lo que supone el mejor registro de la categoría. Además, el cuadro orellut es el que menos disparos ha recibido (68). Estos números reflejan la aportación de todo el equipo al buen rendimiento defensivo del líder de LaLiga Hypermotion, con un repliegue rápido tras pérdida que está siendo fundamental para minimizar las situaciones peligrosas contra su marco. Además, su portero, Matthys, ha intervenido con acierto en situaciones de mano a mano, e incluso en un penalti, parado en la recta final del partido frente al Leganés. Así las cosas, los albinegros encajan de media un gol cada 315 minutos, lo que, unido al buen caudal ofensivo mostrado, explica su balance de 19 puntos de 21 posibles en este inicio de Liga. "Eso dice mucho de todo el equipo, no sólo de Matthys, que obviamente está a un gran nivel. Todos están muy bien con y sin balón y los resultados lo reflejan", reconoció Pablo Hernández tras la victoria en Butarque. La solvencia defensiva del Castellón se está notando de manera más acentuada en Castalia, donde los albinegros no han recibido ningún gol en tres partidos. De esta forma, igualan la racha que tuvieron la pasada campaña con Pablo Hernández al frente entre las jornadas 22 y 26, cuando ganaron en casa a Leganés, Andorra y Deportivo manteniendo la portería a cero.

articles.title: Ireland vs Israel Nations League match will go ahead, coach confirms
articles.summary: The Football Association of Ireland says the team will fulfil the second fixture despite public opposition.
articles.body:
Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson says his team will play their second Nations League football match against Israel on Sunday despite opposition from the Irish public and a public boycott by a player due to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.

“The FAI [Football Association of Ireland] has said we are playing both games,” Hallgrimsson told a news conference in Dublin on Wednesday.

“That was our intention when we came into the camp, and it is still our intention,” the Icelandic coach added.

“We are trying to focus on the football. It is already decided we will fulfil the games.”

Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Hungary on Sunday following a turbulent build-up in which the squad voted to fulfil the fixture after goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu pulled out a day before the game.

Israeli supporters were accused of directing racist chants towards Irish forward Adam Idah and were filmed raising military slogans during the match, but evaded disciplinary action from the competition’s organisers.

The 25-year-old Ireland international, born to a Nigerian father and an Irish mother, was targeted with “monkey chants”, as videos circulating on social media showed, but the fans’ behaviour has gone unpunished by UEFA.

An Israeli supporter also led chants about his country’s military from the stands as he attempted to brush aside the team’s drubbing on the football pitch.

According to reports in the Irish media, UEFA confirmed that racist abuse by Israeli fans towards Idah occurred, but that the matter cannot be investigated because the protocols were not followed by Irish players and officials.

Ireland face Austria on Thursday in Dublin before their designated home match against Israel, which will be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia.

During Sunday’s match in Debrecen, Ireland’s players wore black armbands in recognition of all the lives lost to Israeli attacks in Gaza and bowed their heads as the Israeli national anthem was played at the near-empty stadium.

The teams skipped the traditional pre-match handshakes and did not exchange pennants.

Ireland’s first-choice goalkeeper, Gavin Bazunu , was the only player who publicly opted out of the fixture and posted a statement on social media, saying he felt “it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel”.

Hallgrimsson said on Wednesday the Irish players would again wear black armbands during the second fixture and bow their heads during the Israeli anthem.

articles.title: El Gobierno británico carga contra el Manchester City: "Pueden ser expulsados de la Premier League"
articles.standfirst: La ministra de deportes, Lisa Nandy, calificó el asunto como "muy serio"
articles.summary: La ministra de deportes, Lisa Nandy, calificó el asunto como "muy serio"
articles.body: La decisión de la Premier League de declarar culpable al Manchester City de las irregularidades financieras investigadas durante años ha provocado también la reacción del Gobierno británico. Lisa Nandy, ministra de Deportes, calificó este martes el caso como un asunto "increíblemente serio" y subrayó las importantes consecuencias que podría tener para el club si las acusaciones terminan siendo confirmadas tras el proceso de apelación. En declaraciones a la BBC, Nandy incidió en la gravedad del comunicado publicado por la Premier League y recordó que el Manchester City todavía tiene derecho a recurrir la decisión. "Es un asunto increíblemente serio. El comunicado de la Premier League es muy crudo, aunque el Manchester City tiene el derecho a apelar", señaló. La ministra quiso, en cualquier caso, evitar pronunciarse antes de que concluya el procedimiento. "No quiero adelantarme a ningún proceso de apelación, y tienen derecho a una audiencia justa. Pero lo que sí puedo decir es que la sanción máxima es realmente muy grave", afirmó. Nandy puso el foco precisamente en las posibles consecuencias de una eventual confirmación de los cargos. "Es decir, un club puede ser expulsado de la Premier League si se confirman este tipo de acusaciones, con enormes repercusiones, obviamente, para todos", añadió. La representante del Gobierno británico también aprovechó sus declaraciones para reclamar unas normas financieras claras y una aplicación homogénea de las mismas. "Por lo tanto, creo que la cuestión más importante es cómo nos aseguramos de tener reglas claramente entendidas, que se respeten y se apliquen de manera consistente, y que podamos actuar con rapidez cuando se infrinjan", concluyó.

articles.title: Jaume Jardí hace historia en Primera RFEF
articles.standfirst: El zaragocista se ha convertido en el jugador con más victorias desde su creación
articles.summary: El zaragocista se ha convertido en el jugador con más victorias desde su creación
articles.body: La victoria del Real Zaragoza frente al Ibiza no fue una cualquiera para Jaume Jardí. El catalán se ha convertido en el jugador con más triunfos en Primera RFEF desde que su creación en 2021. El de Reus suma ya 80 alegrías repartidas entre su actual club y los anteriores como el Castilla, Racing de Ferrol y Nástic de Tarragona. El extremo superó en la lista a Álvaro Bustos y Kevin Presa, que habían alcanzado las 79 victorias en la división de bronce del fútbol español. Ese buen hacer y experiencia en la categoría unido a su calidad es lo que llevó a Lalo Arantegui a firmarlo rápidamente para este curso. Apenas le han bastado cinco jornadas para ser uno de los pilares fundamentales de este Real Zaragoza. Jardí lleva ya dos dianas y media y dos asistencias que han resultado clave para catapultar al equipo blanquillo hasta la segunda posición, solo por detrás del filial del Villarreal que cuenta con un punto más. El catalán buscará seguir aumentando ese registro este domingo en el derbi contra el Teruel en el Ibercaja Estadio. Precisamente, en el último partido en casa, fue el propio Jardí el encargado de anotar el tanto del triunfo tras una asistencia de Ureña, quien viene de lograr un doblete en Ibiza.

articles.title: Lane Johnson is proving he remains elite in final season with Eagles
articles.summary: Lane Johnson leads all NFL offensive tackles in pass-block win rate, proving he remains an elite anchor during his final Eagles season
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have several offensive problems to address after scoring seven points in Monday night's loss to the Chicago Bears . Lane Johnson is not one of them.

Johnson is spending his final NFL season doing what he has done throughout a decorated career: neutralizing opposing pass rushers and providing stability at right tackle. Through three games, the six-time All-Pro leads all offensive tackles with a 97.2% pass-block win rate, according to Pro Football Focus. Denver Broncos left tackle Garett Bolles ranks second at 97%, followed by Minnesota Vikings right tackle Brian O'Neill at 96.6%. Johnson's continued placement among the league's best tackles is especially valuable for an Eagles offensive line that has undergone significant changes.

Philadelphia entered the season without Landon Dickerson and has since moved Cam Jurgens to left guard while installing Drew Kendall at center. With the interior still developing chemistry, Johnson has remained the trusted veteran on the right side.

Johnson remains dominant in pass protection

Johnson has played 136 offensive snaps and earned a 74.8 overall PFF grade, ranking 15th among 69 qualified offensive tackles. His 83.4 pass-blocking grade ranks third at the position.

More importantly, Johnson has surrendered only one pressure without allowing a sack or quarterback hit. He has also been flagged for just one penalty. His 68.1 run-blocking grade ranks 26th among tackles, but his overall work confirms he can still perform at an elite level. Philadelphia's offense has struggled to establish consistency through three weeks. Jalen Hurts has dealt with uneven protection, the running game has disappeared for long stretches, and the unit scored only once against Chicago.

None of that can be pinned on Johnson. Even in his final season, the 36-year-old remains one of the NFL's premier pass protectors and the most dependable member of Philadelphia's reshuffled offensive line.

The Eagles' challenge is finding enough stability around him before his remarkable career reaches its conclusion.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Puka Nacua, Justin Jefferson, And More
articles.summary: There are a variety of injuries that will impact fantasy football in Week 4. Here’s how fantasy managers can adjust to win their matchups.
articles.body:
There has been no easing of injuries across the NFL. The latest big name to be lost for the season is De'Von Achane, who suffered a torn ACL last week for the Dolphins. There are several other impactful injuries at various positions, so let's highlight some of them and decide what action to take in fantasy football. For those who need reinforcements, check out our Week 4 waiver wire targets .

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Puka Nacua , WR, Los Angeles Rams

Nacua (hip) missed the last two games for the Rams. With them sporting a 1-2 record, head coach Sean McVay said that he is hopeful that Nacua will play during their Week 4 matchup against the Eagles. Their pass catching options are getting thin with tight end Terrance Ferguson suffering an ankle injury last week that will likely sideline him against Philadelphia .

Week 4 fantasy outlook: Even if Nacua has a limited snap count, he must be started in all fantasy leagues if he returns.

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Nico Collins , WR Houston Texans

Like Nacua, Collins missed the last two weeks for his team. Also, like Nacua, his head coach DeMeco Ryans is hopeful that Collins will return to face the Cowboys on Sunday. Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has struggled with Collins out, throwing just one touchdown pass over the last two games.

Week 4 fantasy outlook: The Cowboys have allowed the second-highest completion rate and the 12th-most yards per target in the NFL. If Collins is cleared to return, he should be started in all leagues.

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Breece Hall , RB, New York Jets

Hall suffered a thigh injury that forced him to leave the Jets' Week 3 loss to the Lions. He did not return to the game and is being considered as week-to-week , meaning he likely won't take the field on Sunday against the Bears. That should create more opportunities for Braelon Allen , who is one of the top waiver wire options at running back.

Week 4 fantasy outlook: Allen is a viable flex option in 12-team leagues for however long Hall is sidelined.

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Justin Jefferson , WR, Minnesota Vikings

Jefferson sat out the second half of last week's matchup with the Buccaneers because of a sprained left ankle. Tests results were encouraging and he is not considered to have a long-term injury . There is even a chance that he plays Sunday against the Dolphins. He already has two touchdowns this season, matching his mark from last year.

Week 4 fantasy outlook: The Dolphins are among the worst defenses in the league, allowing 28.7 points per game. If Jefferson is cleared to play, he can dominate this matchup.

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Travis Etienne Jr. , RB, New Orleans Saints

Etienne was the Saints' prized offseason acquisition after he recorded at least 1,000 rushing yards in three of his first four seasons in the league. However, they will now have to play without him for at least Week 4 as he will miss some time with a hamstring injury. In his absence, Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller should lead the Saints' backfield.

Week 4 fantasy outlook: There is no timetable yet for Etienne's return, so Kamara is worth adding in most leagues. His pass-catching prowess leaves him with more fantasy appeal than Miller, especially in PPR formats.

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Mike Evans , WR, San Francisco 49ers

Evans seems to be living on the injury report this year. He hasn't missed a game yet, but he suffered another ailment in Week 3 when he had a rib strain against the Cardinals. He did catch a touchdown before departing and is considered as day-to-day heading into the 49ers Week 4 battle with the Broncos .

Week 4 fantasy outlook: It's concerning that Evans has left two games early with injuries already. However, with all the injuries that the 49ers have at wide receiver, he is worth starting in fantasy if he is cleared to play.

Fantasy Football Week 4 Injuries: Jalen Coker , WR, Carolina Panthers

Coker has a 27.3% target share for the Panthers on his way to posting 18 receptions for 222 yards and two touchdowns. He is now dealing with a quadriceps injury, although he could still take the field against the Lions on Sunday. If there is any concern about his injury, though, the Panthers could be cautious and rest him with their bye coming in Week 5.

Week 4 fantasy outlook: If Coker is cleared to play, he is an excellent fantasy option against a Lions team that allows the most passing yards per game in the league and continues to deal with key injuries to their secondary.

articles.title: Turkish referees' chief arrested in corruption investigation
articles.summary: The head of Turkey's referees' committee is detained along with six others as part of an investigation into corruption. head of Turkey’s referees committee,...
articles.body:
The head of the Turkish referees' body has been arrested as part of a police investigation into corruption.

Turkish justice minister Akin Gurlek said the investigation focused on "claims regarding interference in the formation of referee classifications, assignments, scoring and appointment processes, as well as rule examinations".

Ferhat Gundogdu, the president of the refereeing body, his vice-president and another five people are those arrested.

Gurlek said police also searched homes, workplaces and offices.

"We will resolutely continue our fight for clean football so that allegations damaging trust in Turkish football are brought to light, those responsible are held accountable before the law, and football is associated with the effort, competition and sportsmanship on the pitch," Gurlek said.

The Turkish Football Federation (TFF) said police inspected the VAR room at its headquarters in Istanbul on Tuesday.

The federation denied reports that digital material had been deleted before the inspection and subsequently recovered by police.

It said it was cooperating with investigators and would file criminal complaints over false reports and social media posts.

In November 2025 the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) suspended 149 referees and assistant referees after an investigation found hundreds of professional match officials in the country had betting accounts.

Some 29 people were arrested in the sprawling scandal, including 14 footballers.

However, Gurlek did not make any link between last year's betting scandal and the current investigation.

articles.title: Un campeón de la Premier no se acostumbra a la vida después del fútbol: "No estaba preparado"
articles.standfirst: Kasper Schmeichel admite que el retiro forzado por una lesión le está resultando difícil de gestionar
articles.summary: Kasper Schmeichel admite que el retiro forzado por una lesión le está resultando difícil de gestionar
articles.body: Kasper Schmeichel está descubriendo que hay una parte del fútbol para la que no estaba preparado: la vida después del retiro. El guardameta danés, campeón de la Premier League con el Leicester en 2016 e hijo del mítico Peter Schmeichel, tuvo que 'colgar los guantes' la pasada temporada después de una carrera de dos décadas por una lesión en el hombro. La retirada no fue una decisión que tomara por voluntad propia. Los médicos le advirtieron de que sería muy complicado volver a competir al máximo nivel y, ante ese escenario, el portero puso punto final a su carrera tras dos temporadas en el Celtic. Ahora, varios meses después, reconoce que está teniendo dificultades para adaptarse a la vida lejos del fútbol. “Estoy lidiando con el aburrimiento”, admite Schmeichel, que ya ha comenzado a prepararse para su siguiente etapa y ha obtenido los títulos necesarios para convertirse en entrenador. Su objetivo es claro y desea volver a formar parte del mundo del fútbol cuanto antes. El danés incluso reconoce que estar desempleado le está resultando estresante después de haber vivido durante 20 años con las exigencias propias de un futbolista profesional. “Con tres hijos, básicamente soy un conductor de Uber a tiempo completo”. Schmeichel asegura que no estaba preparado para el cambio que supone pasar de ser futbolista profesional a tener que construir una nueva vida lejos de los terrenos de juego. Una transición especialmente complicada cuando, como en su caso, la retirada llega por elección que no es propia.

articles.title: Guardiola rompe su silencio: "Lo superaremos juntos"
articles.standfirst: El técnico reacciona ante lo que está sucediendo en la entidad cityzen
articles.summary: El técnico reacciona ante lo que está sucediendo en la entidad cityzen
articles.body: En medio de la incertidumbre que sigue rodeando al Manchester City por el proceso abierto por la Premier League, Pep Guardiola lanzó un contundente mensaje de respaldo a la entidad y a sus aficionados, dejando claro que su compromiso con el club permanece intacto. El técnico catalán quiso dirigirse directamente a la afición 'cityzen' de todo el mundo con unas palabras cargadas de apoyo y sentimiento de pertenencia. "Quiero que todos y cada uno de los aficionados del Manchester City en todo el mundo sepan que estoy aquí; más que nunca", afirmó Guardiola en sus redes sociales. Lejos de tomar distancia ante uno de los momentos más delicados de la historia reciente del club, el entrenador dejó claro que mantiene una confianza absoluta en la estructura que ha liderado el proyecto durante los últimos años. "Siempre he estado y siempre estaré detrás de mi club, de mi propietario, de mi presidente, de Ferran, de los jugadores, del personal, de Enzo y de vosotros, nuestros aficionados únicos", aseguró. Guardiola remató su mensaje con una declaración que rápidamente se ha convertido en un símbolo de unidad para el entorno del club: "Dejadme ser claro: lo superaremos juntos". Las palabras del técnico refuerzan la línea que ha mantenido desde que comenzaron las investigaciones sobre el City. El catalán nunca ha ocultado su respaldo a la entidad y ha defendido en repetidas ocasiones la gestión de la directiva encabezada por Khaldoon Al Mubarak y Ferran Soriano.
